This was the frantic, exhausted worry of a commander who had been holding a crumbling dam together with her bare hands, watching the water rise until her fingers bled.
There was a heaviness in her gaze, a shadow of fatigue that even her divine aura couldn’t fully mask.
"Thank fucking lust... you are finally back here," she said, her voice lacking its usual melodic perfection, sounding instead like a weary sigh.
"Clearly," Rex snapped.
His voice was a jagged wreck, a low, gravelly rasp that felt like he’d been swallowing broken glass.
He sat up fully, the movement causing a sharp, biting ache in his spine, a reminder of the temporal trauma he’d endured.
"Don’t state the obvious, you fucking bitch."
"It’s fucking annoying." He wiped a hand across his face, his eyes burning with a restless, predatory energy.
"How long?
Give it to me straight NOW."
"Long enough that pulling your consciousness into this realm required more effort than the laws of this domain should allow," Lustia replied, her eyes searching his face.
"The external influence on the island... it was tearing at the fabric of the connection."
"It was making the bridge between your world and mine unstable, like a rope fraying under a mountain’s weight..."
"I have been fighting to keep you anchored.
Rex felt a surge of irritation, a hot prickle of anger beneath his skin.
"Fighting...?
Fighting what?"
"The fucking wind?" He stood up, his massive frame casting a long, intimidating shadow against the warm stone.
"Give me a fucking number, Lustia."
"I didn’t come here for a goddamn lecture on the weather."
"How long have I been out?!"
"AND WHAT’S GOING ON!?"
"I do not have a clean number to give you, Rex!" she countered, her voice rising with a rare flash of frustration.
"And that is not an evasion."
"It is the goddamn truth!
Time is no longer a straight line here."
"It is a shattered mirror...
Since the moment you... since the moment the chaos began, the flow has been erratic."
"It has been moving even less predictably than usual."
Rex let out a sharp, cynical bark of a laugh, though there was no humor in it.
He paced the stone floor, his heavy footsteps echoing like hammer blows.
’Fuck’s sake...
I go in for a fucking good time and wake up in a temporal nightmare...’
"So let me get this straight," Rex growled, turning back to her, his eyes flashing with a dangerous, pissed-off light.
"You dragged me into your own sanctuary, into your fucking home, and you’re telling me you can’t even tell me how much time has bled away while I was unconscious?"
"You’ve got the power of a goddess, and you’re as lost as a blind man in a storm?"
Lustia stepped toward him, her expression softening but her eyes remaining intense.
"Hear me out just for a sec..."
"I can tell you that to me, it felt like the passage of most of a night," she said, her voice dropping to a serious, weighted tone.
"But I can also tell you that even that feeling is a lie."
"The sensation of time is unreliable right now, Rex."
"The very foundation of ’duration’ is warping.
And that is exactly what you need to understand before we go any further."

chapters.title: Chapter 867. I Choked A Goddess For Not Answering Fast Enough (I’m Mad ASF!)
paragraphs: Rex stood, his massive frame uncoiling with a predatory grace that belied the sheer amount of trauma his body had just endured. He could feel his infinite regeneration working in the background, a silent, invisible army of cells rushing to seal microscopic tears and stabilize his neurochemistry.

It was a successful recovery, but the "success" came with a heavy asterisk; his muscles felt dense and heavy, as if they had been forged in a furnace and then plunged into ice. His body wasn’t just healed; it was recalibrated after a massive, violent load.
He wasn’t concerned about the comfort of the domain. He cared about the truth.
"What external influence?" he demanded, his voice cutting through the amber light like a serrated blade. "And don’t give me that ’unstable’ bullshit again."
"What is actually out there?"
Lustia opened her mouth to respond, her eyes flickering with a momentary hesitation.

"Be precise, you fucking goddess of a lustful bitch," Rex growled, stepping into her personal space. The sheer heat of his presence seemed to challenge the divine aura she radiated. "I don’t have the patience for metaphors or any of that bullshit anymore because I’ve felt stupid now!"
"Give me the raw data!" Rex gritted his teeth. "What is hitting the island?!"
She met his gaze, refusing to flinch, though he saw the way her fingers tightened almost imperceptibly at her sides.
"A divine presence," she said, her voice dropping into a solemn, heavy register. "But it is not mine..."
"It is not the patron deities of the Apostle network; those bastards are content to watch from the sidelines, exerting a passive, distant influence."

"This is... quite different... this is something active. " Lustia crossed her arms. "Something sustained and something that has been digging its fingers into Aethelgard’s foundational layer and pulling."

A cold, sharp sensation washed over Rex, the specific, chilling dread that comes when a man realizes his entire understanding of the battlefield has just been rendered obsolete. His mental map of the world was being shredded and reassembled in real time.
"For how long," he said, the words coming out as a low, dangerous rumble.
"That," she replied, her voice wavering just a fraction, "is the complicated part."
Rex stared at her, his eyes narrowing into slits of pure, focused intensity. He could feel the mark of lust on his wrist still thrumming, a frantic, dying heartbeat of white light.
"How long has this influence been operating?" he repeated, his patience fraying like a rope under tension. "I’m not asking for a feeling, Lustia."
"I’m asking for a timeline!"
"I am not certain," she admitted, and the admission seemed to weigh a ton. "The very nature of the influence makes a standard duration assessment nearly impossible."
"It defies the logic of linear progression."
"Because the influence is temporal," Rex stated, the realization hitting him with the force of a physical blow.
He wasn’t just experiencing a headache; he was experiencing a collision of eras.

Lustia looked at him with a weary, almost pitying expression, the look of a teacher who had spent an hour explaining a concept only to realize the student had already grasped the terrifying reality of it.
"Yes," she said, her voice a grim confirmation. "Because the influence is temporal."
"Say that again," Rex commanded, his voice dropping to a deadly, quiet hiss. He stepped even closer, his shadow swallowing her. "Say it fucking slowly."

"Because my brain is already trying to skip ahead to the part where this shit gets ugly, and I want to make sure I heard the actual words and not just the version my mind is hallucinating to make sense of this madness."
Lustia took a breath, her eyes locking onto his with unflinching gravity. "Sigh..."

"A god with authority over time has been applying a ’working’ to the island you are standing on," she said, enunciating every syllable as if each were a heavy stone dropped into a well. "A divine manipulation of the temporal flow."
"And that working is the reason your sense of how long things have taken... why your very existence is currently out of sync with everyone else on Aethelgard."
"That is not ’slower,’" Rex spat, a flash of pure, unadulterated fury crossing his face.
He slammed a fist into his open palm, the sound echoing like a gunshot through the silent hall. "That is just calmer!"
"It’s a distortion! It’s a fucking lie!" Rex stomped the ground hard. "I didn’t ask for a slowed-down reality, you fucking bitch!"
"And I didn’t ask to be a ghost in my own timeline!"
"Then stop expecting a version of this that is going to feel calm to you!" Lustia snapped back, her divine composure finally cracking under the pressure of his rage.

The air between them crackled with tension, the golden light of the domain flickering wildly. "I am choosing to speak with calm because one of us needs to maintain a sense of reality, and you have already made it abundantly clear which one of us that is not going to be!"

Rex stood in the center of Lustia’s sanctuary, but he no longer felt like a guest or even an apostle. He felt like a predator whose territory a ghost had breached. This wasn’t the hot, adrenaline-fueled rage of a battlefield, nor the sharp, tactical frustration of a failed maneuver.

This was something far more primal and terrifying: the deep, glacial, soul-crushing anger of a man who had just realized the very ground he stood on was a lie. He had been playing a game where the rules were being rewritten by an invisible hand, and he was the only one who hadn’t been given the new manual.
The air in the domain began to vibrate, not with divine music, but with the sheer, suffocating pressure of Rex’s killing intent.
He didn’t walk; he launched. In four explosive, predatory strides, he bridged the gap between them.
Before Lustia could even draw a breath to offer another measured, "calm" explanation, Rex’s massive, calloused hand shot out like a striking viper.
CRACK.

His fingers clamped around her throat. It wasn’t a clumsy strike or a desperate grab; it was a precise, suffocating grip, the flat, overwhelming force of a man who had decided that words were no longer sufficient and that the conversation now required the language of violence.
He lifted.

With a guttural grunt of pure, unadulterated power, Rex hauled her upward. Lustia’s feet left the warm stone floor by half a meter, her divine robes fluttering uselessly in the sudden vacuum of her own breath.

She hung there, suspended by the sheer strength of his arm, staring down at him with an expression that defied the history of her realm. It was the look of a goddess being physically dominated by her own apostle, a look of profound, jarring shock.
"EXPLAIN!" Rex roared, the sound tearing from his lungs like a landslide.
His eyes were no longer human; they were pits of dark, swirling fury. "EXPLAIN EVERYTHING, YOU DIVINE BITCH!"
"NO MORE POETRY! NO MORE ’CALM’! GIVE ME THE RAW, BLOODY TRUTH!"
He tightened his grip, his thumb pressing into the soft tissue of her neck, forcing a small, pained whimper from her lips.
"WHICH ONE WAS IT?!" he bellowed, his voice vibrating in her very bones. "WHICH COCKY, OVERSIZED PIECE OF DIVINE SHIT THOUGHT THEY COULD REACH INTO MY WORLD AND START TWISTING THE FUCKING CLOCK?!"
"WHICH GOD THOUGHT THEY COULD TOUCH SOMETHING THAT BELONGS TO ME?!"
His rage was a physical thing, a dark aura that seemed to bruise the very light of the domain.
"DON’T TEST ME, LUSTIA!" he hissed, his face inches from hers, his breath hot and smelling of iron and dominance. "YOU THINK BECAUSE YOU RULE THIS PLACE THAT YOU’RE SAFE?"
"IF YOU DON’T START GIVING ME NAMES, I WILL TEAR THIS ENTIRE DOMAIN APART PIECE BY PIECE!"
"I WILL SNAP YOUR DIVINE NECK JUST TO SEE IF THE BLOOD RUNS GOLD OR RED!"
"I DON’T GIVE A FLYING FUCK IF YOU’RE A GODDESS; IF YOU’RE STANDING IN THE WAY OF THE TRUTH, YOU’RE JUST ANOTHER BODY FOR ME TO BREAK!"
Lustia flinched, her eyes widening in genuine, mortal terror. A small, choked gasp escaped her as the pressure on her windpipe intensified, a sharp, stinging pain radiating through her throat.
For the first time in eons, she felt the terrifying sensation of vulnerability. She felt the crushing weight of a man who had transcended the need for divine permission.
Her hands flew up, her slender, elegant fingers wrapping around his massive, bulging forearm. She wasn’t trying to pry him off; she knew she couldn’t break that grip even if she tried.

She was merely holding on, anchoring herself to the only solid thing left in a world that was melting into temporal chaos, her knuckles white as she struggled to maintain her composure while her throat burned under his iron command.
"Aggghh... gacckk..."

chapters.title: Chapter 868. Convenient Would Mean I Look Competent, This Isn’t That
paragraphs: "Rex," she gasped, the word a strained, melodic thread of sound fighting through the crushing pressure of his hand.
Her eyes searched his, not with the gaze of a superior, but with the desperate focus of someone trying to navigate a storm. "Rex... put me down... so I can tell you... before the words... fail me."
She wasn’t just asking for air; she was asking for the dignity required to speak the truth.
"You had a goddamn domain full of warning signs available to you!" Rex’s voice didn’t explode this time; it dropped into a low, vibrating register of pure, concentrated venom.
It was the sound of a predator deciding exactly where to bite. "You had months. You had every single conversation we’ve ever had in this fucking space."
"And the first time the truth reaches my ears is after the damage is done? After the world has already started shifting under my feet?"
’She’s lying,’ a dark voice hissed in the back of his mind. ’She’s hiding the scale of it to keep you from losing your mind.’
’She’s treating you like a tool that needs to be kept in its box.’
"I did not know either!" Lustia finally snapped, her voice cracking with a sudden, sharp vulnerability.
Her fingers dug into his forearm, her divine essence flickering like a dying candle. "Not until the last several hours of this... this nightmare!"
"I am not hoarding secrets like a common politician, Rex!"
"I found this the same way you are finding it now by clawing through the wreckage, except I found it while trying to reach you through a connection that was actively fighting me!"
"That is incredibly convenient," Rex spat, his eyes narrowing. "A goddess who is just as surprised as her apostle..."
"It makes the whole ’divine authority’ thing look a little fucking flimsy, doesn’t it?"
"IT IS NOT CONVENIENT!" Lustia roared back, and for the first time, the mask of the serene goddess shattered completely.
The air in the domain shivered, a shockwave of golden energy rippling outward from her as her true power flared in indignation. "Convenient would be a lie that makes me look competent!"
"Convenient would be a story where I am in control!"
"This reality makes me look like a fool who nearly lost her most precious anchor and didn’t even see the tide coming until it was at her throat!"
She glared at him, her chest heaving, her eyes burning with a fierce, wounded pride. "If I wanted ’convenient,’ Rex, I would have given you a beautiful, polished myth..."
"But instead, you are getting the ugly, jagged truth!"

Rex stared at her, his jaw working, the muscles in his neck still corded like steel cables. He held her there for one more agonizing second, letting her feel the absolute weight of his displeasure, letting the silence stretch until it was a physical pressure.
Then, he released her.

He didn’t just let go; he threw her forward. It wasn’t a strike meant to break bone, but it was a violent, dismissive shove, a physical manifestation of the fact that his patience was a finite resource, and she was currently bankrupting him.

Lustia tumbled through the air, but she didn’t fall like a mortal. She moved with a liquid, predatory grace, her feet touching the stone with a soft thud as she transitioned the momentum into a perfect, upright landing.
She straightened her robes, her breath still coming in shallow, sharp bursts, and looked at him with a gaze that was no longer apologetic but grimly resolute.
"The Mark," she said, her voice regaining its strength, though it remained heavy with gravity.

She pointed a trembling finger toward his wrist, where the Mark of Lust was finally beginning to settle from its frantic, blinding white back into a dull, throbbing glow. "It is reacting to the trauma.
"It is doing exactly what it does when the system’s connection to your biological anchor is under extreme external pressure."
"The pressure wasn’t just magic, Rex... The pressure was the temporal influence itself."
Rex looked down at the Mark, his mind racing, trying to reconcile the physical sensation of the ache with the cosmic scale of her words.
"The influence was affecting me specifically," he countered, his voice hard. "It felt like it was targeting my very soul."
"No," Lustia corrected him, her voice dropping to a whisper that carried more weight than a shout. "The influence was affecting Aethelgard."
"You were affected because you are a part of it."
"You are a part of the fabric. And that is the horror of it, Rex..."
"A temporal working at a divine scale doesn’t hunt individual targets like a predator... It doesn’t pick you out of a crowd."
She looked up at the swirling, amber sky of her domain, her expression one of profound dread.
"It affects the substrate. It changes the very ground that all targets exist within."
"It isn’t changing you, Rex... it is changing the definition of when you are."

Rex looked down at his hands, his knuckles still white, his breath still coming in heavy, jagged plumes that seemed to cut through the divine air of the domain. He felt a profound sense of vertigo, as if the very concept of "now" had become a slippery, unreliable thing.
The Mark on his wrist was still thrumming, a frantic, rhythmic pulse that felt like a trapped bird beating its wings against his skin. But slowly, the frantic tempo began to decelerate.
It was the specific, gradual settling of a biological system receiving the signal that the immediate threat had passed the alarm was being silenced, but the dread remained.
"The God of Time," Lustia said, her voice cutting through the heavy silence like a funeral bell.
She didn’t look at him; she looked through the very fabric of the reality they stood upon. "That is the designation."
"The deity who holds the temporal domain within this world’s divine framework."
"The one who dictates the flow, the rhythm, and the decay of all things."
Rex turned his gaze toward her, his eyes hard and cold as flint.
"The God of Time," he repeated.

He said it slowly, with the flat, terrifyingly calm delivery of a man who was mentally checking every single piece of his life against this new, monstrous variable. He wasn’t just repeating the name; he was weighing it, testing its weight to see if it would crush him.
"Yes," she whispered.
"And this... this entity... has been operating on Aethelgard," Rex stated, his voice dropping into a low, dangerous rumble.
"Yes," she confirmed, her eyes finally meeting his, filled with a sorrow that seemed ancient.
"Without my knowledge," Rex said, the words tasting like ash in his mouth.
A flash of that dark, violent rage flickered in his eyes again. "Without a single god, or apostle, or ’all-seeing’ entity noticing that the very foundation of our existence was being tampered with."
"Without anyone’s knowledge, Rex!" Lustia countered, her voice rising in a desperate attempt to make him understand the scale of the deception. "That is the genius, the absolute horror of it!"
"The temporal influence is specifically engineered to operate below the threshold of consciousness."
"It is a ghost in the machine... The people of Aethelgard have had no way to identify it as an external force because the influence doesn’t feel like an invasion."
"It doesn’t feel like a storm or a war or a god’s hand. It feels like... the passage of time itself."
"It feels like the sun rising and the sun setting... it’s worse that it feels like breathing."
Rex felt a sickening lurch in his gut. A cold, visceral realization began to settle in his bones, more brutal than any physical wound he had ever sustained.
"So every person on that island," Rex said, his voice trembling with a suppressed, lethal fury, "every man, woman, and child... they’ve all been living inside a lie?"
"They’ve been trapped inside a divine mechanism, and they’ve just been calling it an ordinary morning?"
"Yes," Lustia said, her voice barely audible.
"And I have been one of them," Rex spat, the realization hitting him like a physical blow to the solar plexus.
’I was a puppet in a play where the stage was moving while I was dancing,’ he thought, his mind racing back through the recent past, replaying every moment through this new, distorted lens.

"Building the Underlayer. Bleeding in the dirt to fight Apollo. Sitting in that goddamn meeting room, watching the tension coil in the air, watching Valentina’s face fracture when Celestina’s name came out of Apollo’s mouth... all of it."
"Every triumph, every struggle, every drop of blood spilled... it was all happening inside a bubble..."
"We weren’t standing on solid ground."
"We were floating at a god’s whim."
He felt a sudden urge to strike something, to shatter the very air, to break the invisible walls of the temporal cage that had been holding him.
"Not entirely," Lustia said, stepping toward him, her hands reaching out as if to steady him, though she didn’t quite touch him.
Her expression was one of intense, focused gravity. "You were not entirely a prisoner, Rex."
"There are parts of you, parts of your will, that the influence could not fully synchronize."
"And that is the part that matters. That is the part that changes everything."
She paused, her eyes searching his, waiting for the storm in his gaze to settle just enough to receive the killing blow of the truth.

"But you have to hear the shape of the thing first," she warned, her voice trembling with the weight of what was coming. "You have to understand the architecture of the lie, or the part that matters... the part that will decide our fate... will not make any sense at all."

"It makes the whole ’divine authority’ thing look a little fucking flimsy, doesn’t it?"
"IT IS NOT CONVENIENT!" Lustia roared back, and for the first time, the mask of the serene goddess shattered completely.
The air in the domain shivered, a shockwave of golden energy rippling outward from her as her true power flared in indignation.
"Convenient would be a lie that makes me look competent!"
"Convenient would be a story where I am in control!"
"This reality makes me look like a fool who nearly lost her most precious anchor and didn’t even see the tide coming until it was at her throat!"
She glared at him, her chest heaving, her eyes burning with a fierce, wounded pride.
"If I wanted ’convenient,’ Rex, I would have given you a beautiful, polished myth..."
"But instead, you are getting the ugly, jagged truth!"
Rex stared at her, his jaw working, the muscles in his neck still corded like steel cables.
He held her there for one more agonizing second, letting her feel the absolute weight of his displeasure, letting the silence stretch until it was a physical pressure.
Then, he released her.
He didn’t just let go; he threw her forward.
It wasn’t a strike meant to break bone, but it was a violent, dismissive shove, a physical manifestation of the fact that his patience was a finite resource, and she was currently bankrupting him.
Lustia tumbled through the air, but she didn’t fall like a mortal.
She moved with a liquid, predatory grace, her feet touching the stone with a soft thud as she transitioned the momentum into a perfect, upright landing.
She straightened her robes, her breath still coming in shallow, sharp bursts, and looked at him with a gaze that was no longer apologetic but grimly resolute.
"The Mark," she said, her voice regaining its strength, though it remained heavy with gravity.
She pointed a trembling finger toward his wrist, where the Mark of Lust was finally beginning to settle from its frantic, blinding white back into a dull, throbbing glow.
"It is reacting to the trauma.
"It is doing exactly what it does when the system’s connection to your biological anchor is under extreme external pressure."
"The pressure wasn’t just magic, Rex...
The pressure was the temporal influence itself."
Rex looked down at the Mark, his mind racing, trying to reconcile the physical sensation of the ache with the cosmic scale of her words.
"The influence was affecting me specifically," he countered, his voice hard.
"It felt like it was targeting my very soul."
"No," Lustia corrected him, her voice dropping to a whisper that carried more weight than a shout.
"The influence was affecting Aethelgard."
"You were affected because you are a part of it."
"You are a part of the fabric.
And that is the horror of it, Rex..."
"A temporal working at a divine scale doesn’t hunt individual targets like a predator...
It doesn’t pick you out of a crowd."
She looked up at the swirling, amber sky of her domain, her expression one of profound dread.
"It affects the substrate.
It changes the very ground that all targets exist within."
"It isn’t changing you, Rex... it is changing the definition of when you are."
Rex looked down at his hands, his knuckles still white, his breath still coming in heavy, jagged plumes that seemed to cut through the divine air of the domain.
He felt a profound sense of vertigo, as if the very concept of "now" had become a slippery, unreliable thing.
The Mark on his wrist was still thrumming, a frantic, rhythmic pulse that felt like a trapped bird beating its wings against his skin.
But slowly, the frantic tempo began to decelerate.
It was the specific, gradual settling of a biological system receiving the signal that the immediate threat had passed the alarm was being silenced, but the dread remained.
"The God of Time," Lustia said, her voice cutting through the heavy silence like a funeral bell.
She didn’t look at him; she looked through the very fabric of the reality they stood upon.
"That is the designation."
"The deity who holds the temporal domain within this world’s divine framework."
"The one who dictates the flow, the rhythm, and the decay of all things."
Rex turned his gaze toward her, his eyes hard and cold as flint.
"The God of Time," he repeated.
He said it slowly, with the flat, terrifyingly calm delivery of a man who was mentally checking every single piece of his life against this new, monstrous variable.
He wasn’t just repeating the name; he was weighing it, testing its weight to see if it would crush him.
"Yes," she whispered.
"And this... this entity... has been operating on Aethelgard," Rex stated, his voice dropping into a low, dangerous rumble.
"Yes," she confirmed, her eyes finally meeting his, filled with a sorrow that seemed ancient.
"Without my knowledge," Rex said, the words tasting like ash in his mouth.
A flash of that dark, violent rage flickered in his eyes again.
"Without a single god, or apostle, or ’all-seeing’ entity noticing that the very foundation of our existence was being tampered with."
"Without anyone’s knowledge, Rex!" Lustia countered, her voice rising in a desperate attempt to make him understand the scale of the deception.
"That is the genius, the absolute horror of it!"
"The temporal influence is specifically engineered to operate below the threshold of consciousness."
"It is a ghost in the machine...
The people of Aethelgard have had no way to identify it as an external force because the influence doesn’t feel like an invasion."
"It doesn’t feel like a storm or a war or a god’s hand.
It feels like... the passage of time itself."
"It feels like the sun rising and the sun setting... it’s worse that it feels like breathing."
Rex felt a sickening lurch in his gut.
A cold, visceral realization began to settle in his bones, more brutal than any physical wound he had ever sustained.
"So every person on that island," Rex said, his voice trembling with a suppressed, lethal fury, "every man, woman, and child... they’ve all been living inside a lie?"
"They’ve been trapped inside a divine mechanism, and they’ve just been calling it an ordinary morning?"
"Yes," Lustia said, her voice barely audible.
"And I have been one of them," Rex spat, the realization hitting him like a physical blow to the solar plexus.
’I was a puppet in a play where the stage was moving while I was dancing,’ he thought, his mind racing back through the recent past, replaying every moment through this new, distorted lens.
"Building the Underlayer.
Bleeding in the dirt to fight Apollo.
Sitting in that goddamn meeting room, watching the tension coil in the air, watching Valentina’s face fracture when Celestina’s name came out of Apollo’s mouth... all of it."
"Every triumph, every struggle, every drop of blood spilled... it was all happening inside a bubble..."
"We weren’t standing on solid ground."
"We were floating at a god’s whim."
He felt a sudden urge to strike something, to shatter the very air, to break the invisible walls of the temporal cage that had been holding him.
"Not entirely," Lustia said, stepping toward him, her hands reaching out as if to steady him, though she didn’t quite touch him.
Her expression was one of intense, focused gravity.
"You were not entirely a prisoner, Rex."
"There are parts of you, parts of your will, that the influence could not fully synchronize."
"And that is the part that matters.
That is the part that changes everything."
She paused, her eyes searching his, waiting for the storm in his gaze to settle just enough to receive the killing blow of the truth.
"But you have to hear the shape of the thing first," she warned, her voice trembling with the weight of what was coming.
"You have to understand the architecture of the lie, or the part that matters... the part that will decide our fate... will not make any sense at all."

chapters.title: Chapter 869. I’ll Tear The Seconds Out Of His Throat, Very Reasonable Threat
paragraphs: Rex fell into a silence so heavy it felt as though the gravity in the domain had tripled. He didn’t move; he didn’t even seem to breathe.
He just stood there, a monolith of simmering, lethal realization.
"I... I fucking get it now..." he whispered, but the whisper held the vibration of a tectonic plate about to snap.

"The six months," he said, his voice cracking like dry earth. "That’s the bullshit everyone keeps saying. ’It’s been six months.’ ’We’ve had six months of progress.’ ’The timeline is six months.’ There is no way... there is no fucking way it has already been six months..."

Lustia watched him, her heart aching for the man who was currently dismantling his own sanity. She saw the way his hands began to shake, not from fear, but from a violent, kinetic energy that needed to be released, a need to reach out and throttle the very concept of time itself.
"Everyone around me has been referencing six months," Rex continued, his voice rising in a terrifying, rhythmic cadence. "Elizabeth. Valentina. The resource access. The research timelines."
"Six months of archives... Six months of documented research..."
"I have been operating on a subjective timeline that does not correspond to the reality of the world! I’ve been living in a lie of duration!"
"Yes," Lustia said, her voice a soft anchor in his rising storm.
"Because the island’s temporal substrate has been manipulated!" Rex roared, the sound echoing off the divine walls like a thunderclap.

"Because Celestina Von Starlight contracted with the God of Time," Lustia said, her voice gaining a sharp, clinical edge to combat his raw emotion. "And the specific term of that contract was a temporal influence on Aethelgard’s foundational layer."
"It was designed to allow Celestina to manage the engagement timeline at a level she could never achieve through conventional operational planning."
"She didn’t want to follow the clock, Rex... She wanted to own it."
Rex stood perfectly still. The air around him began to distort, a shimmering heat haze born of his sheer, unbridled killing intent.
’A puppet,’ he thought, the word screaming in the dark corridors of his mind. ’I wasn’t a leader...’
’I wasn’t a warrior... I was a goddamn marionette...’
’Every struggle, every drop of blood, every moment of growth... it was all just a rehearsal in a theater controlled by a woman who wanted a better schedule.’
"She could accelerate or decelerate the timeline," Rex said, his voice now unnervingly quiet, the kind of quiet that precedes a massacre.
"More specifically," Lustia added, "she could introduce what I would describe as a loop architecture."
"A temporal working that causes a defined period to repeat or extend without the people within it registering the repetition."
"You could live a thousand years in a single afternoon, and you would never know you were walking in circles."
"Time loop," Rex spat, the words sounding like a curse.

"With the potential for a time reset as its full expression," Lustia said, her eyes wide with the gravity of the horror. "If Celestina had achieved the specific conditions she required before the working reached its maximum expression, Aethelgard would have entered a reset state."
"Everything that had occurred within the working’s duration would have been undone."
"The people on the island would have returned to the state they were in at the working’s beginning... a total, violent erasure of progress."
Rex turned his head slowly to look at her. His eyes were bloodshot, burning with a madness that was purely, beautifully vengeful.
"With no memory of what had occurred," he said, the realization settling into his marrow like ice.
"Correct... with no memory of what had occurred," she confirmed.
"Including the Underlayer’s reconstruction," Rex growled, his hands curling into fists so tight his nails drew blood from his own palms.
The red droplets fell to the floor, bright and visceral against the divine stone.
"Including every development you have produced since the work began," she said. "Every alliance, every technological leap, every scar you earned..."
Rex’s aura suddenly exploded. It wasn’t just energy; it was a roar of pure, unadulterated hatred.
He looked up, not at Lustia, but at the very heavens, as if he could see through the layers of reality to the golden, mocking face of the God of Time itself.
"YOU COWARDLY, SHIFTING PIECE OF DIVINE SHIT!" Rex screamed at the sky, his voice a jagged blade of fury. "YOU THINK YOU CAN PLAY WITH US LIKE WE’RE NOTHING?!"
"YOU THINK YOU CAN FOLD OUR LIVES LIKE PAPER JUST TO SUIT YOUR FUCKING SCHEDULE?!"
"I SWEAR TO EVERYTHING HOLY AND UNHOLY, IF I EVER GET MY HANDS ON THAT CLOCK-WATCHING BASTARD, I WILL TEAR THE SECONDS OUT OF HIS THROAT!"
"I WILL BREAK THE VERY CONCEPT OF ’FOREVER’ UNTIL TIME ITSELF BLEEDS!"
He turned back to Lustia, his face a mask of brutal, desperate demand. The tension was so thick it felt like it could be sliced with a knife.
"Say the rest of it," Rex commanded, his voice low and lethal, his eyes boring into hers. "Do not make me pull the list out of you one item at a time, Lustia."
"Do not treat me like a child who needs to be coddled."
"Tell me everything. Tell me exactly what that bitch would have stolen from us."
"Tell me everything the reset would have taken!"

Lustia stared at him, her gaze unwavering even as the sheer, violent pressure of his aura threatened to crack the very foundation of her domain. She saw the madness in his eyes, the primal urge to reach up and strangle the concept of causality itself.
She knew there was no way to soften this blow. To offer him comfort now would be a second insult, a lie to wrap around a truth that was already jagged enough to kill.
She chose to be the surgeon. She would cut deep, she would be precise, and she would not flinch when the blood started to flow.
"Mara and Marceline’s pregnancies," she began, her voice steady despite the storm raging before her. "Gone... Not just lost, Rex, but completely erased..."
"They would have reverted to the moment before conception, meaning those children would never have been ’unborn’; they would simply never have existed."
"They would be ghosts of a timeline that never happened."
Rex’s jaw tightened so hard a small, sickening crack echoed in the silence. A single vein throbbed violently in his temple.

"Every maximum bond you have forged since the anchor point of this working would have reverted," Lustia continued, her voice gaining a grim, relentless momentum. "The connections, the souls entwined... they would have snapped back to whatever shallow desire existed at the moment the loop began."
"Several of the women you have fought beside, women you have bled for, would have been strangers to you.
"They wouldn’t just have forgotten you; they would have never even met you."
She watched a flicker of agony cross his face, a silent scream of a man realizing how much he had to lose.
"Lily’s telepathic link? Severed."
"The Underlayer’s entire governance structure? Dissolved into chaos."
"Mordecai’s submission? Reverted to defiance."
"The Legion purge? Undone, leaving the rot to fester once more."
"Pavellia’s reconstruction review? A dream that never woke."
"And Elizabeth..." Lustia swallowed hard, her eyes softening for a fraction of a second before hardening again. "Elizabeth’s pregnancy. All of it... All of it is gone..."
"And the most brutal part, Rex... the most goddamn cruel part... is that everyone involved would have simply woken up in a version of Aethelgard where none of it had ever happened."
"They would have no reason to mourn, because to them, there was nothing to mourn."
"They would be happy in their ignorance, while you would be the only one left standing in the wreckage of a life that was stolen from you."
The silence that followed was not empty. It was heavy, suffocating, and thick with the scent of ozone and impending catastrophe.
Rex didn’t roar. He didn’t scream.
He didn’t even move. He stood like a statue carved from the very essence of fury.
But the air around him was changing. This wasn’t the hot, explosive rage of a soldier in the heat of battle, the kind of anger that makes a man swing a sword harder or scream a war cry.
This was something far more terrifying. This was a cold, structural anger.
It was the deep, tectonic shifting of a man who realized he had been building a cathedral on a foundation of shifting sand, only to find that the sand was being moved by the hand of a god.

’They were playing with us,’ his mind whispered, a dark, rhythmic chant that echoed the pounding of his heart. ’They were playing with our lives, our children, our very souls... like pieces on a board.’
’We weren’t living...’
’We were being managed...’
’We were being curated.’
The realization settled into his marrow, turning his blood to liquid ice. He wasn’t just angry at Celestina.
He wasn’t just angry at the God of Time. He was angry at the very fabric of reality for allowing such a deception to exist.
He felt a profound, existential vertigo, a sense that the ground beneath his feet was no longer solid but a thin, fragile membrane stretched over an infinite, mocking void.
He was no longer just a man fighting for survival; he was a man who had realized he was a character in a story written by a liar, and he was finally ready to tear the pages out.

chapters.title: Chapter 870. I’m Not A Piece On Her Board, I’m The Glitch In Her System
paragraphs: "She knew exactly what the fuck I was building!" Rex’s voice didn’t just rise; it tore through the air, a jagged, violent sound that seemed to physically bruise the silence.
He began to pace, his movements predatory and restless, like a caged beast sensing the bars of its cell. "She wasn’t just playing politics!"
"She wasn’t just ’managing’ things!"
"She knew the Underlayer’s reconstruction was the single most significant strategic goddamn development on this entire island in a generation!"
"She knew we were finally gaining real, tangible ground!"

He stopped, spinning on his heel to face Lustia, his eyes burning with a terrifying, incandescent light. "And she went and contracted with the God of Time to produce a reset that would wipe it all out!"
"She was going to hit the fucking ’undo’ button on our lives just to keep her own goddamn hands clean!"
"She was very close, Rex," Lustia said, her voice a calm, chilling contrast to his volcanic fury.

She didn’t flinch as his aura lashed out, a psychic whip of pure resentment. "The Ignivara operation, the geological attack, the combined pressure of the Underlayer’s war declaration and the Legion’s surface operation... you saw them as separate fronts in a war."
"But they weren’t... They were the ingredients..."
"They were the specific, calculated combination designed to produce the exact emotional and strategic crisis state that the reset condition required."
Rex felt a cold sweat break across his brow. His mind was a whirlwind of fury and sudden, sickening clarity. "What was the fucking reset condition, Lustia?!"
"Don’t dance around it! Tell me the goddamn trigger!"

"The temporal working’s reset anchor was tied to the Apostle network’s psychological state," Lustia explained, her eyes fixed on his, refusing to let him look away from the horror. "Specifically, the collective despair of the network’s senior members."
"The working was programmed to monitor the emotional threshold of the leadership."
"When that despair reached a point defined as the ’point of no return’ for Aethelgard’s survival... the reset would have activated automatically."
"It was a failsafe for her... A way to wipe the slate clean the moment the pressure became too much to control."
Rex’s mind suddenly flashed back to the meeting room. The air in his memory felt just as heavy as the air in the divine domain.

He saw Valentina’s face, that hollow, haunting silence when Apollo uttered that name. He saw Morwenna, her eyes brimming with a betrayal so deep it looked like physical pain as she looked at her oldest friend.
He remembered the knowledge system holder, the sheer, agonizing tension of a man ready to argue that thirty years of history might be a goddamn lie.
’We were the fuel,’ Rex thought, a bitter, hysterical laugh bubbling in his throat. ’Our grief, our confusion, our heartbreak... we were just the fuel meant to ignite the reset.’
"We were close," Rex whispered, the realization hitting him like a hammer to the ribs.

"Very close," Lustia confirmed, her voice heavy with the weight of the ’almost.’ "If that meeting had continued in the direction it was moving before you stepped in, before you spoke, the threshold would have been reached within approximately forty minutes."
"You were standing on the edge of a precipice, Rex..."
"One more minute of tension, one more minute of despair, and the world would have folded in on itself.
"Forty fucking minutes," Rex growled, his voice dropping to a low, lethal vibration.
He slammed a fist into his palm, the sound like a bone snapping. "Forty minutes... I stood in that room and talked..."
"I played the diplomat because I didn’t want to watch a network I had spent a goddamn year building leverage over tear itself apart over a single name."
"I was trying to save the network..."

He paused, his breath hitching, a raw, guttural sound of pure agony escaping his chest. "I didn’t know... I didn’t know I was also talking a goddamn deity out of erasing my own bloodline before they were even fucking born to conquer!"
"I was fighting for stability while she was waiting for us to break so she could erase the evidence!"
"You did not know," Lustia said, stepping closer, her voice filled with a desperate need to bridge the chasm of his rage. "That does not make what you did any less the thing that mattered, Rex."
"Intention is not the only measure of an action’s weight."
"You would not have phrased it that way if you had known, but you would have done the same thing."
"You would have stepped into that fire just the same, because the truth was correct for reasons that had nothing to do with the God of Time."

Rex turned his gaze to her, and for a moment, the sheer intensity of his stare was enough to make the divine realm tremble. His eyes weren’t just angry; they were wounded, bleeding with the fury of a man who had been cheated out of his very existence.
"Do not tell me what the fuck I would have done," Rex hissed, the words dripping with a lethal, condescending venom. "Do not you dare try to hand me comfort dressed up as certainty."
"Do not try to soothe the beast, Lustia... Not tonight... Not when the world is a lie and the gods are nothing but fucking thieves."
Lustia held his gaze, her eyes steady and unflinching. She didn’t offer a hollow apology, didn’t cower from the sheer, violent pressure of his presence.

She didn’t try to smooth over the jagged edges of his fury with platitudes. Rex noted this; he noted the way she stood her ground, the way she accepted his venom without letting it poison her own resolve.
It was a rare, brutal kind of honesty, the kind he respected, even if he currently wanted to tear the world apart to find it.
"Fair," she said, her voice a calm anchor in the middle of his hurricane. "I withdraw the certainty."
"But I keep the comfort..."
"You can refuse both if you want, Rex."
"You can stand in this wreckage alone if that’s what you need."
Rex didn’t answer. He couldn’t.
He just turned his gaze downward, staring at his own hands. They were trembling not with weakness, but with a frantic, kinetic hunger for destruction.

The Mark on his skin, that divine tether that had been screaming in his blood, was finally beginning to settle. The violent, erratic pulsing had slowed, receding back to its baseline rhythm, leaving behind a dull, throbbing ache that felt like a brand of shame.
’A failure,’ he thought, the word tasting like bile and copper in his mouth. ’A goddamn, monumental failure.’
He was Rex Rexilion. He was the man who calculated every variable, the man who saw the board three moves ahead of everyone else, the man who had built an empire out of chaos and blood.
He had planned for wars, for betrayals, for the total collapse of entire political structures. He had accounted for the greed of men and the desperation of kings.
He had mastered the art of the long game.
But he had missed this. He had been so focused on the pieces on the board that he hadn’t realized the board itself was being manipulated by a hand from the heavens.
’How fucking could I have been so blind?’ The thought was a serrated blade twisting in his gut. ’I was playing chess while she was rewriting the rules of the fucking universe.’
’I thought I was the architect, but I was just a tenant in a house she could demolish whenever she felt a draft.’
The humiliation was more visceral than any physical wound. It was a deep, structural rot in his pride.

It condensed into a singular, crystalline point of absolute, murderous intent.
’Fine,’ he thought, his eyes narrowing until they were nothing but slits of burning amber. ’That’s fucking fine...’
’If she wants to play with time, if she wants to treat our lives like a fucking draft that can be erased and rewritten... then let her.’
’Let her think she’s won...’
’Let her think the loop is closed...’
A dark, predatory grin tugged at the corner of his mouth, a smile that held no warmth, only the promise of a reckoning.
’She thinks she owns the clock.’
’She thinks she can reset the board when the game gets too messy.’
’But she forgot one thing about the pieces she’s playing with.’
He clenched his fist so hard that the tendons in his forearm stood out like steel cables, and he felt the familiar, delicious sting of his nails digging into the meat of his palm.
’I’m not just a piece on her board...’
’I’m the fucking glitch in her system...’
’And if the God of Time thinks he can just ’undo’ what I’ve built, then I’m going to find a way to reach up into the heavens and choke the fucking seconds out of his throat...’
’I won’t just survive her reset...’
’I will break the cycle...’
’I will find the seam in her perfect little timeline, and I will rip it wide open until time itself bleeds gold and screams in agony...’
He looked up at Lustia, his eyes no longer just angry but possessed by a terrifying, divine purpose.
"She wants a crisis?" Rex whispered, his voice a low, guttural promise of carnage. "She wants a point of no return?"

chapters.title: Chapter 871. Two Things Stopped The Reset, One Was A Speech, One Was Sex
paragraphs: "What stopped the fucking reset?" Rex demanded.
He didn’t want a lecture; he wanted the mechanics of the miracle. He wanted to know exactly which gear had jammed in the celestial machine to prevent his entire existence from being unraveled.
"Two things," Lustia said, her voice cutting through his tension like a blade. "The first was your speech."
"The specific, calculated intervention you made in that meeting... it produced a psychological shift in the room."
"It moved the collective despair of the Apostles away from the threshold."
"You pulled them back from the precipice just enough to stall the momentum."
Rex’s jaw tightened. He remembered the sweat on his palms, the way he had forced his voice to remain steady while his soul was screaming.
"And the second?"
Lustia paused. She looked at him with a specific, heavy expression, the look of a strategist about to reveal the most volatile variable in a complex equation.
It was a look that signaled a truth that would be difficult to swallow.
"Elizabeth," she said simply. "The pregnancy confirmation... the system event."
Rex froze. The air in his lungs felt suddenly thin. His mind raced back to the hours, the frantic, desperate, almost violent hours he had spent with Elizabeth.

It hadn’t just been passion; it had been a primal, subconscious drive to anchor himself to her, to claim her, to weave their lives together so tightly that nothing could ever pull them apart. They had fought for each other in the dark, their bodies colliding with a ferocity that felt like they were trying to fuse their very souls.
Every thrust, every gasp, and every moment of intense, sweaty intimacy had been a desperate, unspoken prayer to the universe: Let this be real. Let this stay.

"The Desire Authority System’s pregnancy mechanic," Lustia continued, her voice growing more clinical as she parsed the divine physics, "generates a massive resonance event in the divine layer the moment a conception is confirmed."
"That resonance is tied directly to my domain and, more importantly, to your Mark."
"In the specific, volatile conditions the temporal working had created on Aethelgard, that resonance produced a frequency that the working’s architecture simply could not handle."
"It was a discordant note in a perfect symphony."
"The pregnancy sex... it disrupted the working," Rex whispered, the realization hitting him like a physical blow to the solar plexus.
"It disrupted the working’s connection to your specific anchor point," Lustia corrected. "The temporal loop lost its ability to include you in the reset architecture."
"It couldn’t ’find’ you to rewrite you, which meant that when the reset threshold would have been crossed, you would have been standing outside the blast radius."
A cold shiver raced down Rex’s spine. "I would have been the only person on the island with a memory of what had actually occurred."
"A ghost in a world of strangers."
"Yes," Lustia said. "Which is a tactical advantage, certainly, but it is not the same as preventing the reset entirely."
"Walk me through it," Rex commanded, his voice raw.
He needed the gore of the truth. He needed to see the blood on the floor.
"Don’t give me the summary."
"Give me the actual goddamn morning."
"I want to know exactly how close I came to waking up in a world where Elizabeth looks at me like a fucking stranger.
"Where Lily has never even heard the name of the Underlayer."
Lustia took a breath, her eyes darkening. "You would have woken up beside her, Rex."
"You would have reached for her, and she would have pulled away not in disgust, but in the polite, distant way a person looks at someone they have just met."
"To her, you would have been a man she had just shared a bed with, but the history... the years of blood, the shared secrets, the deep, soul-searing bond... all of it would be gone."
"Mordecai would still be governing the Underlayer with his usual incompetence and independence."
"Cassandra and Gorvasha would never have fought you, which means they would never have surrendered to you."
"The Legion’s network would still be lurking in the shadows, intact and reporting every move to Celestina."
"Kregg... Kregg would still be alive."
Rex felt a phantom pain in his chest, as if a hand were squeezing his heart.
"They would think I had lost my goddamn mind," Rex said, a bitter, hollow laugh escaping his lips.
"Or they would think you were a liar," Lustia countered sharply. "A man weaving elaborate, delusional fantasies to claim power."
"Either way, you would have been a man standing alone in a crowd of people who had no idea who you truly were."
"You would have been significantly less effective, less powerful, and infinitely more lonely than you are right now standing here with your bonds intact and your memories sharp."
"But the reset didn’t happen," Rex said, his voice dropping to a low, intense growl. "The clock didn’t strike midnight..."
"Why?"
"Because I was watching," Lustia said, her eyes flashing with a sudden, fierce intensity. "And because losing your anchor point created a massive destabilization in the working structure."
"It left a crack in the divine machinery. And because there was a crack, I was able to exploit it."
"I introduced a counter frequency through the domain connection, and the entire working... it collapsed... and it shattered."
"Well, it’s all thanks to both of you that were having sex like fucking animals..."
"Just like that?" Rex breathed, a mix of awe and fury swirling in his gut. "You found a gap, and you just... you slammed the door on a god’s work?"
"You closed a work that a deity had spent months meticulously constructing?"

"Not ’just like that,’ Rex," Lustia said, and for the first time, he heard the exhaustion in her voice, a deep, soul-weary fatigue that suggested she had been fighting a war on a plane he couldn’t even imagine.
"It cost more than I am going to describe to you in detail tonight."
"The price was... heavy. And the details won’t help you now; they would only make you feel obligated to me in a way that would complicate everything."
"What matters is the result, and what matters is that the structure held."
"What matters even more is that you are standing here, alive and furious, able to scream at the heavens instead of being a man who doesn’t even know he’s lost everything."

Rex let out a breath, but it wasn’t a sigh of relief; it was the ragged, shuddering exhale of a man who had just stared into the abyss and realized the abyss was a goddamn cheat. He felt the weight of the entire situation pressing down on him, the sheer, cosmic injustice of it all.
"The God of Time didn’t just watch," Rex said, his voice dropping into a low, dangerous register that vibrated with a cold, calculating fury. "He contracted with Celestina... A mortal...
"He stepped off his fucking throne and took a direct, operational role in a conflict between mortals, acting as the muscle for one of the parties."
"He didn’t just influence the tide; he jumped into the water and started drowning people."
"Yes," Lustia said, her gaze unwavering.
Rex turned to her, his eyes searching hers for any hint of a lie, any shred of the divine nonchalance that usually accompanied such revelations. "That is not how this works, Lustia."
"That’s not how the fucking universe is supposed to function! You said that right?!"
"The divine framework doesn’t permit direct operational intervention on behalf of individual mortals."
"The whole goddamn Apostle system exists specifically to prevent this!"
"It’s a buffer! It’s designed to allow divine interests to operate through chosen human vessels so the gods don’t have to get their hands dirty!"
"It’s a set of rules meant to keep the cosmic order from collapsing into a chaotic goddamn mess."
"Correct," Lustia said, her voice steady despite the intensity of his interrogation.

"He didn’t just bend the rules," Rex growled, his hands clenching into fists so tight his knuckles turned a ghostly, bloodless white. "He fucking violated the operational code of the divine framework itself. He broke the fundamental law of existence."
"He did," Lustia agreed. "And that is precisely why I was able to counter him."
"To strike back, the counter frequency required me to access a level of power that the divine framework’s normal restrictions usually keep locked away."
"But because his violation of the code suspended those restrictions in both directions, the door was kicked open."
"His transgression provided the very opening I needed to shatter his working."
Rex leaned in, his face inches from hers, his expression one of pure, unadulterated contempt. "What a fucking pussy..."
"He cheated," he spat, the word landing like a slap. "He saw a game he couldn’t win by the rules, so he reached under the table and moved the pieces."
"Yes," Lustia said.
"And what happens to a god who cheats?" Rex demanded, his voice rising, a predatory edge creeping into his tone. "In whatever goddamn court exists for them."
"What is the actual, tangible consequence?"
"Does he bleed?"
"Does he lose a limb?"
"Does his essence fracture? Or is it just the kind of vague, meaningless bullshit gods say to each other to pretend there’s a sense of justice in a universe that doesn’t give a fuck?"
Lustia didn’t flinch. She met his hunger for vengeance with a sobering reality.
"There is a consequence, Rex. But it is slower, more subtle, and far more agonizing than what either of us would prefer."
"The other gods will know. A violation of this magnitude doesn’t just ripple; it screams through the divine layer."
"And in a realm built on power, knowing produces pressure."

But it is slower, more subtle, and far more agonizing than what either of us would prefer."
"The other gods will know.
A violation of this magnitude doesn’t just ripple; it screams through the divine layer."
"And in a realm built on power, knowing produces pressure."

chapters.title: Chapter 872. To Lose The Self Is To Lose The Universe
paragraphs: "That pressure will manifest as restrictions and limitations on what he can do, how much he can influence, and how openly he can exert his will for a significant period of time."
She paused, watching the fury boil in his eyes. "It is not punishment in the way you are picturing it, Rex."
"It is not a lashing or a fall from grace. It is politics."
"Politics," Rex repeated.
The word came out of him with a flat, hollow resonance, dripping with a contempt so thick it was almost palpable. He let out a short, bitter bark of a laugh that sounded more like a snarl.
"He tried to erase my children before they even had a chance to draw breath."
"He tried to unmake my very soul and my entire legacy... and the consequence is politics?"
"He gets a reprimand in a divine boardroom while we’re left to bleed in the dirt?"

"The consequence from his peers is politics," Lustia said, her voice sharpening, her eyes locking onto his with a sudden, piercing intensity that made the air between them hum. "But do not mistake the cosmic scale for the final scale, Rex."
"I did not say that was the only consequence available."

Rex fell into a silence that was heavy, suffocating, and thick with the scent of impending storm. For a long time, he didn’t move; he simply stood there, a predator frozen in the moment before the lunge.
The anger he had been nursing, that jagged, directionless fury that had been tearing at his insides since Lustia first spoke the name of the God of Time, began to undergo a terrifying metamorphosis.

The chaotic, screaming rage of a victim transformed into something else. It shed its heat, losing its frantic, burning energy, and distilled itself into something far more dangerous: a cold, surgical, and absolute focus.

It was the anger of a man who had stopped asking ’Why?’ and had begun asking ’Where?’ He wasn’t just a man who had been harmed anymore; he was a man who had identified a target, and he was already beginning to map out the most efficient way to destroy it.
His eyes, sharp and predatory, locked onto Lustia.
"The Balance Keeper designation," Rex said, his voice unnervingly calm, like the stillness before a landslide. "Celestina’s connection to the God of Time..."
"The contract they formed..."
"Connect the dots for me, Lustia... Don’t leave anything out."
"Yes," Lustia replied, sensing the shift in the air.
"The Balance Keeper’s god and the God of Time," Rex continued, his mind working with the ruthless efficiency of a machine, "they aren’t just allies."
"They are the same god... aren’t they?"
Lustia did not answer immediately. The silence stretched, taut and vibrating with tension, until it became an answer in itself.

"They are allied," Lustia finally said, choosing her words with divine precision. "The specific divine designations are not identical, but the god who granted Celestina the Balance Keeper authority and the God of Time are operating from the same strategic position."
"They share a singular, terrifying objective: the preservation of what they call the world’s fundamental equilibrium."
"And reincarnators," Rex said, a dark, knowing smirk ghosting his lips, "are what they define as the ’disruption’ to that equilibrium."
"We are the grit in the gears..."
"We are the anomaly that needs to be sanded down.
"Correct," Lustia said.
Rex lifted his wrist, staring down at the Mark. It looked innocent enough, a mere brand of divinity, but to him, it felt like a bullseye painted in blood.
"He didn’t just cast a wide net over Aethelgard," Rex said, his voice dropping to a low, guttural growl. "He targeted me. Specifically."
"The anchor point you described, the one that the pregnancy disrupted, wasn’t a general temporal working."
"That was a precision strike... It was a working that had been meticulously tuned to my specific divine anchor."
"Yes," Lustia said, her voice uncharacteristically quiet.
"How?" Rex demanded, the calm in his voice cracking just enough to reveal the violence beneath. "How does a god tune a cosmic working to a single, specific anchor?"
"Walk me through the mechanics, Lustia."
"Don’t give me the poetic, ’divine will’ bullshit."
"Give me the mechanics."
"How does a god find a single, microscopic thread inside an entire island and pull it out for special attention?"
Lustia stood tall, meeting his intensity. "He would have needed a sample, Rex."
"A piece of your essence, or something that had been in prolonged, intimate contact with your divine signature before you learned to use Presence Manipulation to mask it."
"The Earthen Authority’s geological anchor... it was broadcasting."
"It was screaming your signature at a scale that a temporal god with sufficient attention could have read, intercepted, and copied without ever needing to stand in the same room as you."
Rex’s eyes darkened. The realization hit him like a physical weight, a cold dread settling in his marrow.
"So that fucking pussy has been watching me because of that power..." Rex gritted his teeth. "He has been studying me since the moment I integrated the gauntlets."
"Since some point after that," Lustia clarified. "The exact date is obscured; the same temporal distortions that made your night so difficult to measure also make his observation window a blur."
"But a working this surgically, this devastatingly specific, does not happen from a single glance."
"He wasn’t just watching you, Rex... He was dissecting you."
"He was reading the rhythm of your soul for a long time before he ever began building the anchor into the reset architecture."
"He was trying to erase me," Rex said. It wasn’t a question; it was a grim, undeniable fact.
"He was trying to erase everything you had built," she corrected. "The structures, the alliances, the power... the entire footprint of your existence."
"It is not quite the same thing as erasing you, but in operational terms, the difference is marginal.
"Marginal?" Rex snapped, the word exploding from him.
He stepped into her space, his presence overwhelming, his eyes burning with a terrifying, singular purpose. "Do not tell me the difference is marginal!"
"There is a version of tonight where you are standing here describing this to a version of me that doesn’t even exist!"
"A version of me that was unmade, wiped clean, replaced by a ghost in a world of strangers!"
"The reset took the part of me that would have been standing here to hear these words!"
"To you, it’s a distinction in a manual, but to me..."
He leaned in closer, his voice dropping to a whisper that carried the weight of a death sentence.
"To me, the difference is total."

Lustia met his gaze, and for a moment, the air in the domain seemed to solidify, becoming heavy and pressurized, as if the very atmosphere were reacting to the sheer gravity of Rex’s conviction. She didn’t flinch at his outburst.
She didn’t offer the hollow comfort of a goddess trying to soothe a mortal’s wounded pride. She simply let the weight of his truth settle between them.
"It is total," she said, her voice resonant and absolute, cutting through the lingering tension like a clarion call. "You are right."
"I chose the wrong word... To lose the self is to lose the universe."
"There is no margin for error when the error is your very existence."
Rex didn’t respond immediately. He turned his head, his eyes sweeping over the vast, ethereal expanse of the domain.

He looked at the warm, amber-hued light that bathed the space, the infinite, unstated reaches of the void that belonged to Lustia and, by the strength of their bond, to him as well. It was a sanctuary, a place of power and respite, yet all he could see was the shadow of the god who had tried to turn this sanctuary into a tomb.
"I am... going to fucking torture and kill him," Rex said.
The declaration didn’t carry the theatrical swell of a hero’s vow. There was no roar, no dramatic flare of energy, no trembling in his voice.
It was delivered with a terrifying, pragmatic flatness, the way a man might state that he intended to eat or that he intended to sleep. It was a logistical fact.
A settled debt. A line item on a list of inevitable conclusions.
Lustia watched him, her eyes tracing the hard lines of his face, the way his muscles were coiled like a spring under tension, ready to snap.
"Yes," she said, her voice a calm anchor in the storm of his intent. "I know."
Rex turned back to her, his eyes narrowing, his gaze becoming a probe, searching for the one thing he hated most in a partner: hesitation.

"And you aren’t going to tell me it’s impossible," Rex stated, his voice dropping into a low, commanding growl. "You aren’t going to stand there with that divine poise and tell me he is too old, or too established, or too far above the station of a reincarnator with a ’lust’ designation."
"You aren’t going to tell me that a mortal, even one with a mark, shouldn’t be reaching for the throat of time itself."
He stepped closer, his presence filling the space between them, demanding an answer that would dictate his next thousand moves. "I want to know right now, Lustia."

"Before I spend a single goddamn hour planning, before I bleed a single drop of sweat or a liter of blood on this path, tell me whether you are going to be the kind of patron who tells me to be reasonable."

chapters.title: Chapter 873. The Fastest Path To Killing A God Runs Through My Bedroom
paragraphs: Lustia felt the heat of his fury, the raw, unyielding hunger for vengeance that burned in his soul. A flicker of something not quite a laugh but a ghost of a smile touched the corner of her mouth, a brief moment of levity that pierced through the exhaustion etched into her features.
"I have never once told you to be reasonable, Rex," she said, her voice gaining a subtle, sharp edge of pride. "Reason is for those who are content with the world as it is given to them."
"I told you the truth about how impossible the task would be."
"I told you how much of yourself you would have to break, how much blood you would have to spill, and how much of the divine order you would have to shatter to reach him."
"But telling you the cost is a different conversation than telling you not to pay it."
Rex exhaled, a long, slow release of tension that felt like a predator settling into a crouch. The tension didn’t leave him; it simply channeled itself into a singular, lethal direction.
"Good," Rex said, a grim, predatory satisfaction settling into his features. "Because if you had tried to tell me to be reasonable, I wouldn’t have listened to you anyway."
"I know that, too," Lustia replied, her gaze softening with a profound, ancient recognition. "It is one of the reasons I chose you."
Lustia sank onto the floor of the domain. It was an uncharacteristic gesture, the goddess lowering herself to the same level as the mortal, but it signaled a shift.
She had moved past the careful management of his emotional volatility; she had moved past the diplomatic caution of a patron. This was no longer a conversation about feelings or consequences.
This was the war council of two beings preparing to commit sacrilege.

"You cannot approach the God of Time as you would approach the Apostle Network or the Legion," she said, her voice carrying the cold authority of a strategist laying out a death sentence. "Those are creatures of flesh and magic."
"The God of Time exists in a dimensional register that your current capability set does not have native access to..."
"To him, you are not a warrior; you are a foreign object attempting to intrude upon a perfect equation."
"I know," Rex said. His voice was flat, devoid of hope or fear, carrying only the grim acceptance of a man who already knew the mountain he had to climb.
"You need more than combat skills," Lustia continued, her eyes luminous with the blue fire of divine knowledge. "Combat skills will get you killed before you even perceive his form."
"You need architectural skills..."
"You need the ability to exist in a dimensional register that is not your native one..."
"You need the ability to compress or mask your presence to a degree that defies human and even divine natural laws..."
"Most importantly, you need a specific adaptation that prevents temporal attacks from unraveling your very atoms before you can swing a blade."
Rex sank down across from her, the movement precise. His mind was already racing ahead, calculating variables like a grandmaster surveying a poisoned chessboard.
"The free skill selection," Rex said, cutting straight to the core. "Elizabeth’s confirmation..."
"The contingency we discussed."
"You have one slot remaining," Lustia said. "It is not enough to claim all three requirements, but it is enough to secure the most critical one.
"Presence Manipulation...?" Rex said. The words felt heavy in his mouth, loaded with the potential for either salvation or absolute annihilation.
"I knew it..." Lustia studied him, her expression unreadable. "You were already thinking about this."
"I was thinking about the divine engagement problem in general terms," Rex corrected, his inner monologue already dissecting the implications. ’I can’t afford to be reactive...’
’If I wait for the threat to manifest, I’m already dead.’
’I have to build the armor before the arrow is fired.’
"The specific application to the God of Time is new... But the skills I was planning to acquire for any divine confrontation are the same ones that apply here."
"You planned for a category of problem before you even knew the specific problem existed," Lustia remarked, and there was something like awe in her tone. "Most people do not think that far ahead."
"Most reincarnators I have watched over centuries solve the problem they can see, only to be slaughtered by the one they could not."

"Most people are not being hunted by something that erases the ground they stand on," Rex snapped, the memory of the reset flashing behind his eyes like a burst of static. "I plan for categories because a category catches things a specific plan misses."
"If I had built my entire strategy around the Legion, none of it would have mattered when a god decided to delete the island beneath my feet."
Lustia nodded slowly. "That is a colder way of thinking than most mortals manage."
"I mean that as an observation, Rex, not a complaint."
"Good," Rex said, his jaw tightening. "Because I wasn’t planning on changing it anyway."
"Then let us speak of the mechanics," Lustia said, returning to the thread with lethal focus. "Presence Manipulation..."
"It allows you to compress, expand, or mask the specific signature that your existence produces across every register simultaneously: physical, energetic, divine, and temporal."
"At full mastery, you can make yourself register as something that poses no threat to a divine perceptive function."
"You could register as something vastly larger than you are to intimidate, or more importantly, you could register as something that simply... is not there at all."
"For the God of Time specifically," Rex interjected, his mind already layering the skill over his tactical vision.

"For approaching his domain without triggering the automated defensive architecture he maintains around it," Lustia clarified. "You must understand: the God of Time’s domain is the one place where temporal attacks do not require a conscious working."
"They are not spells; they are the environment itself..."
"Everything that enters that space enters it under the full, crushing influence of the temporal framework."
"Unless the entering thing is immune," Rex said, his teeth grinding together.

"Unless the entering thing possesses full potential adaptation," Lustia countered. "That skill would absorb the hostile properties of the environment and convert them into operational parameters rather than threats."
"In the God of Time’s domain, Full Potential Adaptation would turn the temporal environment from your greatest enemy into your working medium.
"And how about... dimensional manipulation?" Rex added, the pieces of the puzzle clicking into place with terrifying clarity.
"To reach his domain at all," Lustia concluded. "His domain exists in a dimensional layer that is adjacent to, but not overlapping with, the layer accessible by standard teleportation."
"Dimensional manipulation, combined with your existing teleportation skill, would produce a navigation capacity capable of locating and forcing entry into that adjacent layer."
Rex stared down at his wrist. The Mark glowed faintly against his skin, a constant, pulsing reminder of the divine leash he was trying to snap.
His mind was a battlefield of cold mathematics and raw, bleeding ambition. He ran the numbers again, his mental calculations as precise as a surgeon’s incision.
One free skill selection remaining.
Three fundamental pillars are required to breach the sanctum of a god.
The arithmetic was cruel, and the equation was broken.
In any rational world, Rex was already dead; he was simply a ghost waiting for the universe to realize it.
"The other two skills," Rex said, his voice cutting through the ethereal silence like a blade through silk. "I’m not here for platitudes..."
"Give me the cost."
Lustia didn’t flinch. She met his stare with the unflinching honesty of a mirror.
"The cost is not measured in gold or blood alone, Rex... It is measured in creation."
Rex’s jaw tightened. "Speak plainly."
"You need pregnancies because the energy you need is still far away," Lustia said, each word carrying the weight of a divine decree. "Two more confirmed unions."
"Two more anchors of life to manifest the necessary power."
"One to unlock dimensional manipulation to give you the spatial leverage to tear through the fabric of reality."
"One to unlock full potential adaptation to give you the resilience to survive the crushing weight of eternity."
A muscle jumped in Rex’s cheek. The implications settled over him like a shroud.

This wasn’t just a quest for power; it was a quest that demanded he weaponize intimacy, turning the most primal of human connections into tactical necessities. His inner monologue screamed with a mix of disgust and cold, calculating pragmatism.
’I have to turn my own body into a factory for divine intervention.’
’Every union becomes a transaction, and every moment of passion becomes a siege engine...’
"So," Rex said, the words tasting like ash as he forced them past his teeth.
A dark, twisted smile, one that held no humor, only a grim, terrifying resolve, tugged at the corner of his mouth.
"The fastest path to killing a god," he said, his gaze locking onto hers with the intensity of a predator who had just accepted a poisoned bait, "runs directly through my own bedroom."
