"It allows you to compress, expand, or mask the specific signature that your existence produces across every register simultaneously: physical, energetic, divine, and temporal."
"At full mastery, you can make yourself register as something that poses no threat to a divine perceptive function."
"You could register as something vastly larger than you are to intimidate, or more importantly, you could register as something that simply... is not there at all."
"For the God of Time specifically," Rex interjected, his mind already layering the skill over his tactical vision.
"For approaching his domain without triggering the automated defensive architecture he maintains around it," Lustia clarified.
"You must understand: the God of Time’s domain is the one place where temporal attacks do not require a conscious working."
"They are not spells; they are the environment itself..."
"Everything that enters that space enters it under the full, crushing influence of the temporal framework."
"Unless the entering thing is immune," Rex said, his teeth grinding together.
"Unless the entering thing possesses full potential adaptation," Lustia countered.
"That skill would absorb the hostile properties of the environment and convert them into operational parameters rather than threats."
"In the God of Time’s domain, Full Potential Adaptation would turn the temporal environment from your greatest enemy into your working medium.
"And how about... dimensional manipulation?" Rex added, the pieces of the puzzle clicking into place with terrifying clarity.
"To reach his domain at all," Lustia concluded.
"His domain exists in a dimensional layer that is adjacent to, but not overlapping with, the layer accessible by standard teleportation."
"Dimensional manipulation, combined with your existing teleportation skill, would produce a navigation capacity capable of locating and forcing entry into that adjacent layer."
Rex stared down at his wrist.
The Mark glowed faintly against his skin, a constant, pulsing reminder of the divine leash he was trying to snap.
His mind was a battlefield of cold mathematics and raw, bleeding ambition.
He ran the numbers again, his mental calculations as precise as a surgeon’s incision.
One free skill selection remaining.
Three fundamental pillars are required to breach the sanctum of a god.
The arithmetic was cruel, and the equation was broken.
In any rational world, Rex was already dead; he was simply a ghost waiting for the universe to realize it.
"The other two skills," Rex said, his voice cutting through the ethereal silence like a blade through silk.
"I’m not here for platitudes..."
"Give me the cost."
Lustia didn’t flinch.
She met his stare with the unflinching honesty of a mirror.
"The cost is not measured in gold or blood alone, Rex...
It is measured in creation."
Rex’s jaw tightened.
"Speak plainly."
"You need pregnancies because the energy you need is still far away," Lustia said, each word carrying the weight of a divine decree.
"Two more confirmed unions."
"Two more anchors of life to manifest the necessary power."
"One to unlock dimensional manipulation to give you the spatial leverage to tear through the fabric of reality."
"One to unlock full potential adaptation to give you the resilience to survive the crushing weight of eternity."
A muscle jumped in Rex’s cheek.
The implications settled over him like a shroud.
This wasn’t just a quest for power; it was a quest that demanded he weaponize intimacy, turning the most primal of human connections into tactical necessities.
His inner monologue screamed with a mix of disgust and cold, calculating pragmatism.
’I have to turn my own body into a factory for divine intervention.’
’Every union becomes a transaction, and every moment of passion becomes a siege engine...’
"So," Rex said, the words tasting like ash as he forced them past his teeth.
A dark, twisted smile, one that held no humor, only a grim, terrifying resolve, tugged at the corner of his mouth.
"The fastest path to killing a god," he said, his gaze locking onto hers with the intensity of a predator who had just accepted a poisoned bait, "runs directly through my own bedroom."

chapters.title: Chapter 874. I Don’t Need A Funeral Hymn, I Need Him Permanently Toothless
paragraphs: "It is not the framing I would have chosen," Lustia said, her voice carrying the detached cadence of someone discussing the weather rather than the transactional nature of human intimacy. "But it is not inaccurate either."
"The system you were given ties its most significant unlocks to the specific, primal act of creating life..."
"I did not design that mechanism, Rex..."
"I inherited a domain and a designation with mechanics that were already carved into the bedrock of reality the same way every god inherits the bones of whatever came before them."

Rex stared at her, his mind churning through the implications. The coldness of it, the sheer, mechanical cruelty of a universe that demanded such a price, made something hot and angry coil in his gut.

"You are telling me you did not build the pregnancy mechanic," he said, the accusation sharp enough to draw blood. "You’re telling me you’re just the administrator of a system designed to exploit the most vulnerable parts of human connection."

"I am telling you the Lust domain has always operated on these principles, long before you existed to weaponize it," Lustia countered, her eyes unblinking. "Desire that produces new life carries more metaphysical weight in the divine layer than desire that merely consumes."
"It is a fundamental law of our physics..."
"I simply administer the domain; I did not invent its gravity."
"Convenient administration," Rex muttered.
His inner voice was a snarl. ’A system where power is bought with flesh and seed...’
’It’s obscene... But if this is the currency of gods, I will spend every cent I have until I’m bankrupt...’
"For me, at least."

"I have never pretended the arrangement does not benefit you," Lustia said, her tone shifting to something almost approving. "I would be a poor patron if I did not provide you with the tools to achieve your impossible goals."
Rex didn’t acknowledge the compliment. His focus had already shifted from the cost to the clock.
The enemy wasn’t just a god; it was time itself.
"The timeline," he demanded, leaning forward until he was mere inches from her divine presence. "How long before the God of Time makes another attempt?"
"How long before he decides to erase me along with everything else?"

"I do not know with certainty," Lustia admitted, and for the first time, Rex saw a genuine shadow of uncertainty cross her features. "His violation of the divine framework’s operational code has consequences that ripple through the celestial hierarchy."
"The other gods are now aware that he acted directly, that he bypassed the protocols."
"That creates political pressure and that also creates friction... It will limit his immediate ability to repeat such a blatant transgression."
"So there is a window," Rex said, his voice dropping to a lethal whisper.

"A window," she confirmed. "Its duration depends on two variables: how quickly he can navigate the political fallout among his peers and whether Celestina’s next operational move creates a justification, a divine pretext, for him to act again."
The name Celestina struck Rex like a physical blow. His mind flashed back to the communication crystal, the way it had felt beneath his grip before he crushed it into worthless glittering dust.

He remembered the specific, venomous message he had sent her. It had been a calculated provocation: aggressive enough to force her hand, but measured enough to ensure her response didn’t arrive before he had finished his preparations.
He was playing a game of chicken with a goddess, and the stakes were his own existence.
’I can’t hesitate,’ he thought, his pulse hammering against his ribs like a trapped animal. ’Every second I spend thinking is a second he spends calculating how to kill me...’
’I need those skills...’
’I need those anchors...’
’Now.’
His thoughts pivoted with practiced, ruthless efficiency toward his targets. He had already been mapping them out, analyzing their vulnerabilities, and studying their patterns.
He had been planning them for reasons that had nothing to do with divine warfare—reasons of personal ambition and raw, unadulterated want.
Iris and Aurelia.
The God of Time situation had not changed his targets; it had simply stripped away the luxury of patience. The hunt was no longer about conquest; it was about survival.
"Full potential adaptation," Rex said, the words tasting like iron on his tongue. "What does it do beyond the God of Time’s domain?"
"Give me the full scope, Lustia..." He crossed his arms. "Don’t spare the technicalities."
Lustia straightened, her divine aura flickering with a sudden, sharp intensity. "It does exactly what its name implies, Rex."
"It is the ultimate evolutionary response..."
"Every ability, every spell, and every divine manifestation that an opponent hurls at you, your body and your system will analyze upon first contact."
"They will dissect the fundamental frequency of that attack and integrate the necessary defense into your operational parameters."
"The second time that same ability touches you, you will find yourself adapted to it."
"The adaptation is permanent and it is cumulative..."
"You become a living countermeasure to everything that has ever tried to harm you."
Rex stared at her, his mind already running through his existing toolkit.
"I already have Infinite Regeneration even though it’s a fucking scam," he challenged, his voice rough. "Why would I need both?"
"Because you misunderstand the nature of your own survival," Lustia said, her voice dropping to a cold, pedagogical register. "Infinite regeneration is reactive."
"It heals damage after it has already occurred... It mends torn flesh, knits broken bones, and seals ruptured arteries."
"It is a brilliant tool for enduring a massacre, but it still requires you to suffer the massacre first."
She stepped closer, the blue fire in her eyes burning brighter. "Full potential adaptation is proactive."

"It prevents the damage from occurring in the first place after the initial exposure. And more importantly, adaptation covers what regeneration cannot: ability suppression, designation interference, temporal distortion, and the specific category of divine working that operates on the soul rather than the biological system."
"Infinite regeneration cannot heal a soul that has been rewritten."
A cold chill traced Rex’s spine.
"The God of Time’s attacks operate on the soul," he whispered, the realization sinking in like a poisoned dagger.
"His domain operates on the soul," Lustia corrected grimly. "Everything within his reach is subject to his temporal authority."
"That authority works at a level deeper than biology, deeper than cellular structure..."
"Infinite Regeneration cannot regenerate something that has been temporally altered, something that has been erased from its own timeline.
"You cannot heal what no longer has a history."

Rex sank back into his thoughts, the weight of the revelation pressing down on his shoulders. He could almost feel it: the terrifying sensation of his own existence being unraveled, his memories dissolving into static, his very bones turning to ash not from heat, but from the simple fact that he had never been born.

"Say... I get all three skills," Rex said finally, his voice steadier now, though his eyes remained dark with calculation. "Presence Manipulation, Dimensional Manipulation, Full Potential Adaptation."
"Say I walk into his domain wearing all of them like armor..." Rex held his chin. "What actually happens when I find him?"

"What does killing a god look like in practice? Because I have killed armies, I have killed monsters, and I have killed kings, but none of them were something that has existed as a fundamental constant for two thousand years.
Lustia fell silent. She considered the question with more care than she had given any before.

There was a long, pregnant pause, the kind of silence that precedes a catastrophe. She was weighing how much truth was useful and how much truth was simply too frightening for a mortal mind to process without breaking.
"Gods do not die the way mortals die," she said at last.
Her voice was hollow. "A god’s existence is not merely flesh and bone; it is tied to belief, to conceptual authority, and to the domain they command."
"If you reach him and you damage that body enough, what you produce is not death in the way you are picturing it..."
"You do not produce a corpse."
"Then what do I produce?" Rex demanded.
"You produce a wound to his authority," Lustia said. "His domain destabilizes."
"His grip on reality slips and his ability to act in the mortal layer weakens, sometimes for years... sometimes permanently depending on how thoroughly the wound is inflicted."
"So I cannot kill him the way I killed Kregg and the others, huh?" Rex said, a bitter edge creeping into his voice. "I can’t just drive steel through his heart and watch him bleed out."
"No," Lustia said firmly. "But you can end him functionally."
"A god with no authority and a destabilized domain is not meaningfully different from a dead one to anyone who would have suffered under his continued action."
"The distinction matters to theologians and scholars..."
"It does not matter to Celestina’s next reincarnator target, and it does not matter to the child you and all your maximum bond women are going to have."
Rex’s jaw set. The anger that had been simmering beneath his skin crystallized into something harder, something sharper.
The need for poetic justice died in his throat, replaced by a cold, utilitarian hunger for vengeance.
"Then that is the version I am planning for," Rex said, his gaze fixed on some distant, bloody horizon. "I do not need a poetic ending."
"I do not need to hear hymns sung at his funeral because I need him unable to touch anything I have built... Ever again."
"That is achievable," Lustia said, her expression one of grim respect. "It will be difficult, though."
"It will be excruciatingly costly. And it will almost certainly require far more than the three skills we are discussing tonight."
"But Rex... it is achievable."

chapters.title: Chapter 875. Repeat Until The God Falls, My New Personal Motto
paragraphs: Rex stared at her, his eyes distant, as if he were already standing in the center of a divine storm, calculating the wind resistance of his own soul. He wasn’t arguing with Lustia anymore; he was rehearsing a ritual of slaughter.
"I already have Infinite Regeneration," he said again, but the words were quieter now, stripped of defiance and replaced with the cold, mechanical precision of a general reviewing battle plans.
"I’m not questioning you... I’m stacking."
"Full Potential Adaptation layered over Infinite Regeneration gives me a body that a temporal god cannot damage through anything he has wielded twice."
"The first time he strikes, I bleed, but then... the second time he strikes, he finds I am no longer made of the same substance he intends to break."
His fingers flexed unconsciously, imagining the grip on a weapon. "Dimensional manipulation provides the breach; it gets me through the door and into his sanctum."
"And Presence Manipulation..." A dark, predatory hunger flickered in his gaze. "Presence manipulation keeps him blind."
"It keeps him arrogant and ensures he doesn’t even realize the predator has entered his lair until my blade is already halfway through his throat."
"That is the correct architecture," Lustia said, her voice carrying a rare note of genuine surprise. "You have constructed a fortress of survival in real time, Rex."
"You built it faster than I anticipated all within the span of a single conversation."
"I’ve had plenty of practice building architecture around things that want me dead," Rex countered, a bitter smile ghosting across his lips. H
His inner monologue was a relentless engine of war: ’Build the shield, sharpen the sword, find the throat.’
’Repeat until the god falls.’
"This isn’t a new discipline... It’s just a new opponent." Rex grinned. "The math changes, but the cruelty remains the same."
Lustia studied him for a long moment. The air between them grew heavy, charged with the static of two powerful entities recognizing a monster in the making.
There was something in her expression, a quiet, unsettling respect. She wasn’t looking at a mortal struggling against fate; she was watching a predator assemble a trap that could catch a star.
Rex closed his eyes for a second, visualizing the dominoes.
"The sequence is clear," he said, his voice dropping to a lethal register. "Presence manipulation first..."
"I need to disappear before I become a target."
"Then Iris and Aurelia... I need the anchors, the life force required to fuel the next two unlocks."
"And then, once the foundation is set, I claim Dimensional Manipulation and Full Potential Adaptation..." Rex punches his own fist. "After that... I’ll fucking hunt my prey."
"That is exactly the sequence I would recommend," Lustia said, nodding approvingly. "The presence manipulation serves a dual purpose."
"It also addresses a critical operational gap you have been carrying since the Sable Island integration."
Rex’s eyes snapped open, sharp as flint. "Which gap?
"Your Earthen Authority’s geological anchor," Lustia explained, her tone turning clinical. "It is a paradox..."
"It is one of your most significant power sources, but it is also a screaming beacon."
"To anyone with sufficient divine perceptive capability, that anchor reads as a divine class signature, a flare in the darkness that is completely inconsistent with your chosen cover identities."
"You are trying to walk through a den of wolves while carrying a torch that announces your name."
Rex’s jaw tightened. He had felt the subtle, nagging sensation of being watched, of his power feeling too ’loud’ against the fabric of the world.

"Presence Manipulation allows you to mask that signature," Lustia continued. "You can make it read as something mundane, something harmless, or you can make it vanish entirely, depending on what the situation demands."
"It turns your greatest vulnerability into a ghost."
Rex didn’t respond. His gaze drifted downward, falling on the Mark etched into his skin.

It pulsed with a faint, ominous light, a reminder that every power he gained came with a price in flesh, in blood, and in the lives of those he would claim to fuel his ascension. The war had begun, and he was already measuring the distance to the first kill.
"The system notification," Rex said, his voice cutting through the charged silence like a blade. "The free skill selection... It’s still pending."
"Take it now," Lustia commanded, her eyes fixed on him with urgent intensity. "Don’t hesitate."
"The sooner presence manipulation is woven into your fundamental code, the sooner that screaming beacon of yours becomes a whisper."
"Every second you delay is another second you’re exposed."
Rex didn’t need to be told twice. With a sharp mental flick, he tore open the system’s skill catalog, the ethereal interface bleeding into his field of vision.
[PRESENCE MANIPULATION FULL POTENTIAL]
[COMPLETE CONTROL OVER THE SPECIFIC SIGNATURE THAT YOUR EXISTENCE PRODUCES ACROSS ALL DETECTION REGISTERS SIMULTANEOUSLY.]
[REGISTERS COVERED: PHYSICAL MASS AND HEAT SIGNATURE, ENERGY AND SYSTEM SIGNATURE, DIVINE ANCHOR SIGNATURE, TEMPORAL PRESENCE SIGNATURE, AND SOUL LAYER SIGNATURE.]
[ADJUSTABLE FROM FULL AMPLIFICATION (SIGNATURE READS AS SIGNIFICANTLY LARGER THAN ACTUAL CAPABILITY) TO COMPLETE ABSENCE (NO SIGNATURE IN ANY REGISTER).]
[INTERMEDIATE SETTINGS: CAN MIMIC SPECIFIC SIGNATURES OF KNOWN ENTITIES OR PRODUCE ENTIRELY FABRICATED SIGNATURES.]
[PASSIVE FUNCTION: CONSTANT LOW-LEVEL SIGNATURE MANAGEMENT THAT PREVENTS CASUAL DETECTION OF PRIMARY IDENTITIES ACROSS COVER OPERATIONS.]
[ACTIVE FUNCTION: DELIBERATE SIGNATURE MANIPULATION FOR SPECIFIC TACTICAL APPLICATIONS.]
[COMBINATION WITH SHAPESHIFTING: PRODUCES COMPLETE IDENTITY REPLACEMENT AT BOTH PHYSICAL AND SIGNATURE LEVEL.]
[COMBINATION WITH ENERGY MANIPULATION: EXTENDS SIGNATURE MANAGEMENT TO OBJECTS AND CONSTRUCTS IN CONTACT RANGE.]
[DIVINE APPLICATION: AT FULL MASTERY, SIGNATURE CAN BE COMPRESSED TO MATCH A MORTAL BASELINE, PREVENTING DIVINE PERCEPTIVE FUNCTIONS FROM IDENTIFYING THE PRESENCE AS A DIVINE CLASS ENTITY.]
[FREE SELECTION APPLIED AT NO COST.]
Rex didn’t pause to marvel at the sheer, terrifying scope of the power. He simply locked onto the selection and slammed it home. Execute.

The integration was unlike anything he had experienced before. When he had acquired his other skills, it felt like adding new rooms to a house, a physical sensation of expansion, of weight, of new muscle fiber knitting into his existing frame.
But presence manipulation felt like a violation of a different kind. It felt like a subtraction.

It was as if he had been standing naked in a spotlight his entire life, unaware of the searing heat on his skin, and suddenly, the light began to dim. He felt the raw, pulsing energy of his Earthen authority, the geological weight that made him feel like a mountain beginning to retract, folding inward.

The Mark of Lust, which had always throbbed with a frequency that felt like a heartbeat in the astral plane, began to muffle, its divine resonance dampened. The accumulated ’noise’ of his other full potential skills, the dimensional static, and the temporal echoes all began to collapse.

He sat there in the heart of Lustia’s domain, eyes closed, grimacing as his very essence underwent a violent recalibration. Inside his mind, it was a chaotic storm of data: ’Compress. Muffle. Suppress. Erase.’
He could feel the system forcibly grinding down his divine profile, crushing the jagged peaks of his power into something smooth, something manageable, something quiet.
Finally, the pressure receded. He opened his eyes.
He felt smaller. Not weaker, far from it, but he felt less obvious.

His Earthen Authority was still there, coiled like a sleeping dragon beneath his skin, but the ’smell’ of it was gone. His divine frequency had been compressed into a profile that would now read, to any casual divine observer, as nothing more than an above-average reincarnator with a decent skill set.
He was no longer a flare in the dark; he was a shadow among shadows. Not unremarkable, but precisely calibrated to avoid triggering a god’s defensive paranoia.
"Good," Lustia said, her voice carrying a note of satisfaction as she watched the residual energy dissipate from his body.
"How do I look?" Rex asked. His voice was rough, and there was something almost dry in it—the closest he had come to humor since he had woken up bleeding on her floor.
"Quieter," Lustia replied. "Which, coming from me, is the highest compliment I can offer."
"I have spent centuries listening to apostles broadcast their existence across three different registers like desperate children screaming for attention."
"You have never once wanted to be noticed by the wrong audience..."
"This skill simply allows your instincts to finally catch up to your ambitions."
Rex’s mind immediately pivoted back to the mission. The hunger for the kill was still there, but now it was tempered by a cold, professional patience.
"The Iris and Aurelia timeline," he said, his voice hardening. "How soon can we move?"
"As fast as you can manage without compromising the operation’s other requirements," Lustia said, her gaze turning serious. "The foundation must be flawless, Rex."
"If you rush the fuel, the engine will shatter before you ever reach God’s doorstep."

"I already have Infinite Regeneration," he said again, but the words were quieter now, stripped of defiance and replaced with the cold, mechanical precision of a general reviewing battle plans.
"I’m not questioning you...
I’m stacking."
"Full Potential Adaptation layered over Infinite Regeneration gives me a body that a temporal god cannot damage through anything he has wielded twice."
"The first time he strikes, I bleed, but then... the second time he strikes, he finds I am no longer made of the same substance he intends to break."
His fingers flexed unconsciously, imagining the grip on a weapon.
"Dimensional manipulation provides the breach; it gets me through the door and into his sanctum."
"And Presence Manipulation..." A dark, predatory hunger flickered in his gaze.
"Presence manipulation keeps him blind."
"It keeps him arrogant and ensures he doesn’t even realize the predator has entered his lair until my blade is already halfway through his throat."
"That is the correct architecture," Lustia said, her voice carrying a rare note of genuine surprise.
"You have constructed a fortress of survival in real time, Rex."
"You built it faster than I anticipated all within the span of a single conversation."
"I’ve had plenty of practice building architecture around things that want me dead," Rex countered, a bitter smile ghosting across his lips.
H
His inner monologue was a relentless engine of war: ’Build the shield, sharpen the sword, find the throat.’
’Repeat until the god falls.’
"This isn’t a new discipline...
It’s just a new opponent." Rex grinned.
"The math changes, but the cruelty remains the same."
Lustia studied him for a long moment.
The air between them grew heavy, charged with the static of two powerful entities recognizing a monster in the making.
There was something in her expression, a quiet, unsettling respect.
She wasn’t looking at a mortal struggling against fate; she was watching a predator assemble a trap that could catch a star.
Rex closed his eyes for a second, visualizing the dominoes.
"The sequence is clear," he said, his voice dropping to a lethal register.
"Presence manipulation first..."
"I need to disappear before I become a target."
"Then Iris and Aurelia...
I need the anchors, the life force required to fuel the next two unlocks."
"And then, once the foundation is set, I claim Dimensional Manipulation and Full Potential Adaptation..." Rex punches his own fist.
"After that...
I’ll fucking hunt my prey."
"That is exactly the sequence I would recommend," Lustia said, nodding approvingly.
"The presence manipulation serves a dual purpose."
"It also addresses a critical operational gap you have been carrying since the Sable Island integration."
Rex’s eyes snapped open, sharp as flint.
"Which gap?
"Your Earthen Authority’s geological anchor," Lustia explained, her tone turning clinical.
"It is a paradox..."
"It is one of your most significant power sources, but it is also a screaming beacon."
"To anyone with sufficient divine perceptive capability, that anchor reads as a divine class signature, a flare in the darkness that is completely inconsistent with your chosen cover identities."
"You are trying to walk through a den of wolves while carrying a torch that announces your name."
Rex’s jaw tightened.
He had felt the subtle, nagging sensation of being watched, of his power feeling too ’loud’ against the fabric of the world.
"Presence Manipulation allows you to mask that signature," Lustia continued.
"You can make it read as something mundane, something harmless, or you can make it vanish entirely, depending on what the situation demands."
"It turns your greatest vulnerability into a ghost."
Rex didn’t respond.
His gaze drifted downward, falling on the Mark etched into his skin.
It pulsed with a faint, ominous light, a reminder that every power he gained came with a price in flesh, in blood, and in the lives of those he would claim to fuel his ascension.
The war had begun, and he was already measuring the distance to the first kill.
"The system notification," Rex said, his voice cutting through the charged silence like a blade.
"The free skill selection...
It’s still pending."
"Take it now," Lustia commanded, her eyes fixed on him with urgent intensity.
"Don’t hesitate."
"The sooner presence manipulation is woven into your fundamental code, the sooner that screaming beacon of yours becomes a whisper."
"Every second you delay is another second you’re exposed."
Rex didn’t need to be told twice.
With a sharp mental flick, he tore open the system’s skill catalog, the ethereal interface bleeding into his field of vision.
[PRESENCE MANIPULATION FULL POTENTIAL]
[COMPLETE CONTROL OVER THE SPECIFIC SIGNATURE THAT YOUR EXISTENCE PRODUCES ACROSS ALL DETECTION REGISTERS SIMULTANEOUSLY.]
[REGISTERS COVERED: PHYSICAL MASS AND HEAT SIGNATURE, ENERGY AND SYSTEM SIGNATURE, DIVINE ANCHOR SIGNATURE, TEMPORAL PRESENCE SIGNATURE, AND SOUL LAYER SIGNATURE.]
[ADJUSTABLE FROM FULL AMPLIFICATION (SIGNATURE READS AS SIGNIFICANTLY LARGER THAN ACTUAL CAPABILITY) TO COMPLETE ABSENCE (NO SIGNATURE IN ANY REGISTER).]
[INTERMEDIATE SETTINGS: CAN MIMIC SPECIFIC SIGNATURES OF KNOWN ENTITIES OR PRODUCE ENTIRELY FABRICATED SIGNATURES.]
[PASSIVE FUNCTION: CONSTANT LOW-LEVEL SIGNATURE MANAGEMENT THAT PREVENTS CASUAL DETECTION OF PRIMARY IDENTITIES ACROSS COVER OPERATIONS.]
[ACTIVE FUNCTION: DELIBERATE SIGNATURE MANIPULATION FOR SPECIFIC TACTICAL APPLICATIONS.]
[COMBINATION WITH SHAPESHIFTING: PRODUCES COMPLETE IDENTITY REPLACEMENT AT BOTH PHYSICAL AND SIGNATURE LEVEL.]
[COMBINATION WITH ENERGY MANIPULATION: EXTENDS SIGNATURE MANAGEMENT TO OBJECTS AND CONSTRUCTS IN CONTACT RANGE.]
[DIVINE APPLICATION: AT FULL MASTERY, SIGNATURE CAN BE COMPRESSED TO MATCH A MORTAL BASELINE, PREVENTING DIVINE PERCEPTIVE FUNCTIONS FROM IDENTIFYING THE PRESENCE AS A DIVINE CLASS ENTITY.]
[FREE SELECTION APPLIED AT NO COST.]
Rex didn’t pause to marvel at the sheer, terrifying scope of the power.
He simply locked onto the selection and slammed it home.
Execute.
The integration was unlike anything he had experienced before.
When he had acquired his other skills, it felt like adding new rooms to a house, a physical sensation of expansion, of weight, of new muscle fiber knitting into his existing frame.
But presence manipulation felt like a violation of a different kind.
It felt like a subtraction.
It was as if he had been standing naked in a spotlight his entire life, unaware of the searing heat on his skin, and suddenly, the light began to dim.
He felt the raw, pulsing energy of his Earthen authority, the geological weight that made him feel like a mountain beginning to retract, folding inward.
The Mark of Lust, which had always throbbed with a frequency that felt like a heartbeat in the astral plane, began to muffle, its divine resonance dampened.
The accumulated ’noise’ of his other full potential skills, the dimensional static, and the temporal echoes all began to collapse.
He sat there in the heart of Lustia’s domain, eyes closed, grimacing as his very essence underwent a violent recalibration.
Inside his mind, it was a chaotic storm of data: ’Compress.
Muffle.
Suppress.
Erase.’
He could feel the system forcibly grinding down his divine profile, crushing the jagged peaks of his power into something smooth, something manageable, something quiet.
Finally, the pressure receded.
He opened his eyes.
He felt smaller.
Not weaker, far from it, but he felt less obvious.
His Earthen Authority was still there, coiled like a sleeping dragon beneath his skin, but the ’smell’ of it was gone.
His divine frequency had been compressed into a profile that would now read, to any casual divine observer, as nothing more than an above-average reincarnator with a decent skill set.
He was no longer a flare in the dark; he was a shadow among shadows.
Not unremarkable, but precisely calibrated to avoid triggering a god’s defensive paranoia.
"Good," Lustia said, her voice carrying a note of satisfaction as she watched the residual energy dissipate from his body.
"How do I look?" Rex asked.
His voice was rough, and there was something almost dry in it—the closest he had come to humor since he had woken up bleeding on her floor.
"Quieter," Lustia replied.
"Which, coming from me, is the highest compliment I can offer."
"I have spent centuries listening to apostles broadcast their existence across three different registers like desperate children screaming for attention."
"You have never once wanted to be noticed by the wrong audience..."
"This skill simply allows your instincts to finally catch up to your ambitions."
Rex’s mind immediately pivoted back to the mission.
The hunger for the kill was still there, but now it was tempered by a cold, professional patience.
"The Iris and Aurelia timeline," he said, his voice hardening.
"How soon can we move?"
"As fast as you can manage without compromising the operation’s other requirements," Lustia said, her gaze turning serious.
"The foundation must be flawless, Rex."
"If you rush the fuel, the engine will shatter before you ever reach God’s doorstep."

chapters.title: Chapter 876. He Was Afraid Of Me... A God...? Afraid Of Me? Good
paragraphs: Rex turned his head to meet her gaze, his eyes shining as polished obsidian. There was no anger in his expression, only the flat, dangerous stillness of a predator who had just been given a new variable to calculate.
"I know what I am doing," he said.
The words weren’t defensive; they were a statement of fact, delivered with the absolute certainty of a man who had already rehearsed his own death a thousand times.

"I know you do," Lustia countered smoothly, her voice unruffled. "But you need to understand something: this is the first time you have been operating with a deadline that is defined by someone else’s timeline rather than your own."
"You are no longer the sole architect of this catastrophe."
Rex didn’t flinch. He acknowledged the truth of it with a single, slow nod.
The reality of it settled in his gut like cold lead. He was used to being the storm, the unpredictable variable that crashed through systems.
Now, he was being asked to dance to a rhythm he hadn’t composed.

"That is going to happen more than once before this is finished, isn’t it?" Rex asked, his mind already beginning to map out the contingencies. "Kaeleth is not the only piece on this board that moves without waiting for my permission."
"No," Lustia said, her expression darkening. "He is not."
"Celestina has her own clock, ticking with lethal precision..."
"The other gods watching this situation have theirs, each waiting for a crack in the foundation."

"Even I am operating on a schedule I do not fully control." She paused, a flicker of something resembling genuine strain crossing her features. "Whatever counter frequency I used to break the working drew attention in the divine layer. Attention I am still desperately trying to manage the consequences of."
Rex’s eyebrows shot up, a rare crack in his composure. "You never mentioned that."
"I am mentioning it now," Lustia said with a sharp, almost defensive edge. "I did not want to add another burden to your pile while you were still holding me by the throat."
"It seemed like poor timing."
Rex let out a breath that might have been a laugh if there were any humor left in him. "That is fair."
He meant it, and he noted the mild surprise at his own capacity for concession. He was learning that in this game of gods, pragmatism was more valuable than pride.
"The God of Time," Rex said, shifting the focus back to the threat. "His name was Kaeleth, you say... it doesn’t sound godly at all."
"Indeed... Kaeleth," Lustia answered. "That is his designation in the old language the divine framework uses."

"He has occupied this position for approximately two thousand years. In that span, he has produced three apostles, all of whom are dead." Her voice dropped an octave. "Celestina is not his apostle; she is his contracted partner."
"That distinction is precisely what makes her involvement here a violation of the cosmic order."
"Contracted partner," Rex repeated, testing the words.
They sounded like something far more dangerous than a simple alliance.

"An arrangement that the divine framework does not formally prohibit but one that it strongly discourages," Lustia explained. "Apostles are chosen by the god and empowered through a divine blessing, a gift from above."
"Contracted partners, however, choose the god.
"They empower themselves through the god’s authority in exchange for a specific service."

"The service Celestina provides Kaeleth is simple and brutal: the elimination of reincarnators, whom Kaeleth’s temporal perceptive functions identify as parasites and timeline disruptions that threaten the sanctity of his domain."
"So she is his pest control," Rex said, a grim smile tugging at his mouth.
"She is his ideologically aligned contractor," Lustia corrected. "She performs a service he values deeply in exchange for divine authority she could never access through the standard Apostle system."
"Because the standard Apostle system," Rex interjected, his intellect cutting through her explanation like a scalpel, "would never grant the ’Balance Keeper’ designation for the purpose of genocide."
"The other gods would recognize the pattern immediately..."
"They would refuse to permit a god to officially sanction the systematic hunting of reincarnators, and it would upset the balance."

"Correct," Lustia said, clearly impressed by how quickly he had dissected the divine politics. "The contract arrangement allows him to bypass the god community oversight that every other divine act must endure."
Rex leaned back, his mind racing through the implications. "Three dead apostles in two thousand years is a pathetic record for a god of his caliber."
"What killed them? I want to know if there is a pattern before I decide whether I need to worry about them."
"Two of them died to causes unrelated to their designation," Lustia said. "One died of age; the apostle bond did not extend his mortal lifespan the way some other designations do."
"The second died through betrayal by a rival apostle during a period of open divine conflict two centuries ago." She paused, her eyes locking onto his. "The third is the one that matters to you."
Rex felt a chill crawl down his spine. "Tell me about the third."
"The third apostle attempted to use the temporal authority Kaeleth granted him to alter his own past," Lustia said, her voice hushed. "A personal application, not a sanctioned one."
"Kaeleth’s domain does not forgive that kind of transgression."
"A temporal alteration to an apostle’s own timeline creates a paradox, a load, a wound in reality that the domain itself must absorb to maintain stability."
"The apostle wasn’t killed by a weapon or an enemy. He was simply... unmade by the paradox."
"Erased from existence by the very power he tried to weaponize against fate."
Rex’s eyes gleamed with a newfound, predatory interest. The horror of the story didn’t frighten him; it intrigued him.
"So the domain itself is a weapon that points in more than one direction," he mused aloud. "Good. That is useful."
"If the domain can unmake its own choice for misusing its power, then there may be a way to trick it into unmaking him."
Lustia stared at him for a long moment, recognizing the terrifying implications of his thought process.
"That is an incredibly aggressive read of what most would consider a cautionary tale," she said quietly. "But it is not a wrong one."

Rex rose to his full height, his shadow stretching across the floor like an inkblot. The air between them remained charged, thick with the residue of their confrontation, but the violence had passed, leaving behind something far more dangerous: clarity.
"I want everything," Rex said, his voice dropping into a register of absolute command. "I want every scrap of intelligence you possess regarding Kaeleth’s domain."
"Its dimensional coordinates, its defensive architecture, and the specific temporal mechanics that govern its internal logic."
"I want to know how it breathes, how it reacts to intrusion, and exactly how it enforces its own laws.
"Give me everything."
Lustia stood to meet him, her regal bearing returning, though her eyes remained fixed on his with an unblinking intensity.
"I will give you what I know," she said, her voice steady despite the exhaustion beneath it. "But understand this: some of it will be incomplete..."
"His domain is not merely hidden; it is deliberately obscured from divine observation."
"He has woven it into the folds of causality itself."
"Give me the incomplete version anyway," Rex countered immediately. "I don’t need a perfect map to begin."
"I will fill in the gaps with blood and experience when I arrive."
Lustia’s lips thinned into something resembling a smile—sharp, knowing, and almost challenging.
"When you arrive," she corrected him. "Not if."
Rex met her challenge without blinking. "When."
Lustia searched his face for a long moment. In that silence, the mask of the goddess slipped.

For a heartbeat, she wore an expression she rarely allowed: a warm, vulnerable, almost painfully personal look that transcended the transactional nature of their bond. It was the look of a being who had invested something irreplaceable into a mortal she knew would likely burn the world down.
"He made a mistake," she said softly, the admission carrying more weight than any threat. "Kaeleth made a tactical error."
"He contracted a mortal to handle a reincarnator he should have recognized as something beyond mortal control."
"He violated the divine code; he broke the very laws he represents because he believed he had no other choice."
"He broke them because he was afraid, Rex..."
"He was terrified of what you were building."
Rex stared at her, the implications sinking in.
Fear. A god of time, a being who sees the beginning and end of all things, was experiencing fear because of a single man’s trajectory.
"Good," Rex said. The word was simple, but it carried the promise of inevitable retribution.
He fell silent then, the only sound the low hum of the domain’s ambient energy. He looked at her in the amber glow of her sanctum, and something in his expression shifted.

The raw fury that had consumed him earlier had cooled, but it hadn’t vanished. Beneath the anger and the cold, calculating machinery of his mind, something else emerged, something quieter, more profound.
"You could have handled tonight differently," Rex said suddenly.
His voice wasn’t accusatory; it was observational, like a surgeon noting a flaw in a procedure. "You could have given me the soft version first... eased into the bad news."

"Most of the gods I’ve read about in the archives manage their apostles like precious assets, things to be protected from harsh realities, shielded from the truth until they are strong enough to bear it."
"But you? You gave me the whole truth, raw and ugly, in the correct order..."
"You even included the parts where you nearly failed."

chapters.title: Chapter 877. Stay Serious, I Said, Right After Roasting Her Thigh-Grinding
paragraphs: Lustia didn’t flinch at the memory of his grip on her throat.
"I did nearly fail," she said simply. "Softening that truth would have been a lie..."
"And if I lied to you, you would have discovered it eventually; the truth always finds its way out, and then you would have had a reason to doubt every word I ever spoke."
"I would rather you be angry at the truth than comfortable with a lie."
"Most people would have chosen comfort," Rex said, stepping closer to her.
"I am not most people," Lustia replied, her chin lifting. "And as you have pointed out to me more times than I care to count, usually as a complaint, I am also not most gods."
"It wasn’t always a complaint," Rex murmured, the corner of his mouth twitching. "Tonight, it isn’t one at all."
Lustia watched him, waiting for the blade to drop.
"I mean that," Rex said, his voice gaining a rare sincerity. "I’ve spent a great deal of time treating you as a resource."
"Something to be managed, something useful, something occasionally frustrating but ultimately something to be handled correctly rather than something to actually listen to."

"But tonight..." he paused, searching for the words. "Tonight you sat on the floor of your own domain and handed me the truth, knowing exactly what my hand around your throat was going to feel like before you even opened your mouth."
"That isn’t what a resource does..."
"That is what someone does when they have decided the relationship matters more than their own comfort."
Lustia fell silent. For once, the goddess had nothing to say.
The power dynamic between them had shifted irrevocably; it was no longer master and tool, or goddess and apostle. It was something far more complicated.
Rex took one last look at her, his eyes reflecting a respect that was more terrifying than his wrath.
"I prefer this version of you," he said. "The serious one..."
"Not the warm, teasing thing you perform when you think I need to be managed gently."
"This... Someone who tells me the truth even when the truth makes her look like she nearly lost everything."

The silence that followed Rex’s declaration was heavy, charged with a new kind of understanding. But Rex, ever the predator who knew exactly when to shift tactics, decided to shatter the moment’s gravity with surgical precision.
He took two steps closer, invading her personal space until he could smell the faint, divine scent of her skin. His expression remained deadly serious, his eyes boring into hers.

"And another thing," Rex added, his voice dropping to a husky, dangerous growl. "I prefer this version because she doesn’t immediately start grinding against my thigh every time I finish explaining a tactical problem."
Lustia froze. The regal, composed goddess who had just stood firm against his wrath suddenly appeared as if struck by lightning.

"I... that is a gross mischaracterization of divine enthusiasm!" she stammered, her cheeks flushing a shade of crimson that rivaled the sunset. "I am a goddess of... of... of... profound cosmic energies!
"What you perceive as... as inappropriate physical proximity is merely... residual mana discharge!"
Rex didn’t blink. "Residual mana discharge... Right."
"Yes!" Lustia said, her hands fluttering uselessly in front of her as she tried to regain her dignity. "It is a very scientific phenomenon! "
"Very common in higher dimensions!"

"You wouldn’t understand; it’s... it’s... it’s statistically improbable for a mortal to experience such—" She tripped over her own words, her divine composure crumbling into a heap of nervous babbling. "The alignment of the stars suggests that physical contact is a fundamental necessity for maintaining dimensional stability during periods of high stress!"
"Is that why you were eyeing my belt buckle during the briefing on Celestina’s movements?" Rex asked flatly.
Lustia let out a sound that was halfway between a squeak and a cough. "I was assessing the... the structural integrity of your equipment!"
"For safety purposes! Purely for your protection, Rex!"

Rex simply stared at her for three more seconds of excruciating awkwardness before turning away. He didn’t offer a rebuttal, didn’t laugh, and didn’t acknowledge her increasingly desperate attempts to explain away her obvious arousal.
He simply dismissed her as one would dismiss a malfunctioning piece of equipment.

As he walked toward the edge of the domain’s platform, his mind retreated from her flustered stammering. The comedy of her reaction faded instantly, replaced by the cold, razor-sharp focus that defined his existence.
He left the flustered goddess behind, her nonsensical explanations echoing uselessly in the air.
’Kaeleth,’ he thought, his inner voice as cold as the void between stars. ’You think you can contain a storm by hiring a hunter.’
’You think you can cage time by contracting a killer... But you’ve forgotten what happens when you try to trap something that doesn’t belong to your timeline.’
His mind began to dissect the mechanics Lustia had described. He pictured the paradox load the way reality itself would recoil when forced to swallow its own contradiction.
He could almost feel the phantom pressure of it.
’If the domain punishes the user for breaking time,’ Rex mused, his mental fingers tracing the invisible ley lines of the threat ahead, ’then I don’t need to kill Kaeleth...’
’I just need to make him complicit in his own unraveling...’
’I will make his own authority the rope that strangles him.’
Rex looked at Lustia. "That’s enough of all the yap... you really are worth my respect after helping me with that information... make sure to stay like this if I want it serious."

Something shifted across Lustia’s features, a tremor in the divine porcelain of her composure that Rex had never witnessed before. In all their previous encounters, their conversations had danced between the cold calculus of strategic counsel and the intimate, almost playful teasing she employed when invoking his title as her ’dear apostle.’
But this was not that. This was not the practiced warmth of a goddess maintaining the equilibrium of her chosen vessel.
It was something raw. Something dangerously unguarded.

It was the look of a being who had been caught completely undefended, seen with terrifying accuracy by the one mortal whose perception had begun to matter more to her than the celestial hierarchies she commanded.
"Rex," she whispered.
His name didn’t carry its usual melodic cadence or the teasing lilt that usually rode alongside it. It came out fragile, stripped of its divinity, sounding almost human.
"You don’t have to say anything," Rex said, his voice cutting through the sudden, suffocating intimacy of the moment. "I’m not asking for a confession or a response."
"I’m stating a fact... Because you gave me the truth when it would have been easier to lie, and I believe that level of honesty deserves to be acknowledged."

Lustia turned her head away, unable to sustain his piercing gaze. She looked toward the amber glow of her domain’s light, the divine energy that usually felt like a comforting embrace but now seemed to expose every crack in her armor.

When her eyes finally returned to his, they betrayed her. They held that specific, shimmering brightness, the terrifying luminescence that precedes tears in a being who has spent millennia learning how to suppress every mortal weakness.
"Two thousand years..." she said, her voice cracking like thin ice under pressure. "Two thousand years of existing as something beyond understanding, and no one has ever said that to me."
"Not like that... Not with the weight you put behind it."
"Then it was overdue," Rex replied flatly. His tone wasn’t cruel, but it lacked the softness she clearly craved; he was a man who dealt in certainties, not comforts.

The silence that followed was absolute, a vacuum that seemed to pull the very air from the room. Lustia stood there, a goddess reduced to something achingly vulnerable, while Rex stood before her not as a supplicant but as an equal who had just dismantled her defenses without drawing a blade.

But even as the emotional tension reached its breaking point, Rex’s mind remained a fortress of cold calculation. Behind the rare moment of acknowledgment, the gears of his intellect were already grinding against the implications of what she had revealed.
’Alright... back to that fucking god I need to talk about...’
’Kaeleth,’ he thought, the name tasting like copper and old blood in his mind. ’You think you can play god with the fabric of time itself.’
’You think you can hide behind contracts and ’balance’ while you hunt down the anomalies you can’t control.’

His fingers flexed instinctively, as if already feeling the resistance of a temporal barrier. He could almost envision the domain of the Time God not as a sanctuary, but as a trap lined with paradoxes, waiting to snap shut on anything that moved out of sync with its rhythm.
’Let her weep, let her feel,’ he mused grimly, his inner monologue shifting back to the hunt. ’I’ll give her the truth she deserves...’
’But when I step into that domain, I’m not going there to negotiate or to understand.’
’I’m going there to break the clock. And if Kaeleth thinks he’s seen a monster before, he’s about to learn that some things can’t be erased; they can only be unleashed.’

chapters.title: Chapter 878. I Have My Alibi, My Target, And My Truth... Time To Break Things
paragraphs: Lustia let out a laugh, a short, unsteady sound that cracked like shattering crystal. It was a sound completely devoid of divine composure, almost human in its fragility.
She reached up, wiping at the corner of her eyes with the back of her hand in a raw, unguarded gesture that belonged to someone far younger than the millennia etched into the stones of her domain.

"Look at what you have done," she said, shaking her head as she tried to reassemble her shattered dignity. "I brought you here to warn you, to tell you that a god attempted to erase the very foundation of your existence, and somehow, this is the part of the night that undoes me."
Rex watched her, his expression unreadable, though the intensity in his gaze never wavered.
"I did not plan it that way," he said simply.
"I know," she whispered, a bitter smile touching her lips. "That is exactly why it worked."
The moment of vulnerability passed, sealed away by necessity. Lustia straightened her spine, the goddess reasserting control over the woman.
Then, she began to speak.

She poured out everything she knew about Kaeleth’s domain. She spoke of temporal eddies that could shred a soul into infinite screaming fragments; of defensive architectures woven from crystallized moments of frozen time; and of the way the domain’s gravity didn’t pull at the body, but at the causality of one’s own past.

Rex listened with a flat, systematic attention, the kind of cold, predatory focus he reserved for intelligence briefings where every syllable could mean the difference between a successful kill and a catastrophic failure.
By the time she finished, the incomplete picture was burned into his mind. He saw the map not as a series of locations but as a series of vulnerabilities.
He saw the gaps in her knowledge, the dark spaces where divine sight failed, and he marked them as places where he would have to wade through blood to find answers.

’The temporal mechanics...’ Rex thought, his mind already dissecting her words. ’If the domain operates on a feedback loop of cause and effect, then any intrusion that doesn’t match the established timeline will trigger a cascade failure.’
’I won’t just be fighting guards; I’ll be fighting the very concept of... now.’
’Every step forward will be a war against the universe trying to correct my presence.’
The ambient light of the domain began to shift, the warm amber hues deepening into a bruised purple, signaling that the session was drawing to its inevitable conclusion.
"One more thing," Rex said, his voice cutting through the settling silence.
Lustia turned back to him, her eyes wary.
"You said the reset would have undone everything I built since the working began," Rex said, his mind already calculating the stakes. "The Underlayer’s reconstruction..."
"The blood spilled in Aethelgard and the intelligence extracted from Ignivara..."
"All of it erased."
"Yes," Lustia confirmed, her voice dropping to a solemn register. "Wiped clean as if the last months were never written in the book of fate."
"What is the specific anchor point?" Rex asked, leaning forward, his pupils contracting. "The exact moment from which the reset would have triggered?"
Lustia paused, her lips pressing into a thin line as she searched through layers of cosmic memory.
"The working’s anchor point," she said finally. "The moment the chain became unbreakable.
"The moment Celestina contracted with Kaeleth."
Rex’s jaw tightened. "Which was..."
"Approximately," Lustia said, choosing her words with deadly precision, "six months before the current date as experienced by the inhabitants of Aethelgard."
Rex closed his eyes for a second, the implications crashing over him like a tidal wave. Six months.
Half a year of slaughter, of strategic positioning, of building his empire of bone and steel—all of it hung on a thread that a single divine whim could have severed.
’Six months,’ he thought bitterly. ’Six months of playing chess with destiny, only to realize the board was rigged from the start.’
’Kaeleth didn’t just try to kill me; he tried to make it so I never existed to challenge him.’
’He tried to delete my struggle.’
"But keep in mind... the timeline is currently fucked, so no one... even we didn’t know the real time, so just to make sure, you need to fix it by teaching Kaeleth a lesson."
A cold, murderous resolve crystallized in Rex’s chest. His grip tightened on the armrest of his chair, the wood creaking ominously under the pressure of his strength.
’Let him try to reset the clock again,’ Rex vowed internally, his thoughts turning as sharp as a guillotine blade. ’Next time I step into his domain, I’m not going to play by his rules...’
’I’m going to break the clock, smash the gears, and drag him into whatever fractured reality he thinks he can control.’
’I’ll make him feel every second he tried to steal from me.’

Rex fell into a silence that was not empty but loaded a pressurized stillness that seemed to warp the space between them. His mind was a furnace, burning through data, cross-referencing variables with the ruthless efficiency of a predator calculating the trajectory of a kill.
"The six months everyone keeps referencing," he said finally, his voice carrying the flat, dangerous edge of a blade being drawn from its sheath.
"Yes," Lustia replied, her voice steadying but still carrying the faintest tremor of the vulnerability she had just shown.
"My subjective timeline is significantly shorter," Rex stated. It wasn’t a question; it was a diagnosis of a fundamental flaw in reality.
Lustia nodded slowly, her divine eyes reflecting the complex geometries of the temporal wound she was describing. "Because the temporal working’s influence was not uniform across the island, Rex."
"Time did not flow like a river there; it moved like a storm, swirling around obstacles."
"The working affected people based on their connection to the island’s foundational substrate..."
"And you..." she paused, choosing her words as if walking through a minefield, "...you are connected to that substrate at a divine level through the Earthen Authority."
"That connection created a different relationship to the work’s influence than the standard biological connection of a mortal."
"I experienced the actual time," Rex said, his jaw tightening. "The raw, unvarnished seconds as they truly passed."
"You experienced something closer to it," she corrected gently. "The discrepancy between your timeline and the island’s is precisely what produced the inconsistencies you noticed."
"You were walking through the real world while everyone else was living inside a temporal bubble."
Rex’s mind began to sprint. He replayed every conversation, every piece of paper, every strategic move he had made.
He saw Valentina’s resource authorizations flashing before his eyes. He saw the research timelines laid out in meticulous detail.
He saw the documented history, the very thing that had provided his bulletproof alibi.
"The documented history," Rex said, the realization clicking into place like the hammer of a gun. "The archive entries."
"Elizabeth’s authorization codes... These weren’t just records; they were created within the working’s influenced timeline."
"Yes," Lustia said grimly. "Which means they reflect the island’s experienced time, not the actual time."

"They are consistent within the working’s framework," Rex mused, a cold smile tugging at the corner of his mouth, a smile that promised violence to anyone who dared challenge his logic. "Whether that framework was a legitimate manipulation of reality or a divine deception, the documents exist."
"They are internally consistent and they hold up under any scrutiny."
"Yes," she agreed.
"Which means the alibi works regardless of whether the working’s existence is proven or denied," Rex concluded.

The trap he had built was stronger than he had imagined. Even if Kaeleth revealed the truth of the temporal manipulation, the paper trail would still point to the same conclusion: Rex was exactly where he claimed to be.
"In the sense that the documents exist, are verifiable, and align with the perceived reality of every witness... yes," Lustia said, almost impressed by the ruthless pragmatism of his mind.
Rex looked at her one last time before the domain’s light completed its shift. The amber glow was fading into a deep, obsidian dusk.
The look he gave her wasn’t the transactional glance of an apostle speaking to his goddess. It was something heavier.
An acknowledgment of a shared secret, of a vulnerability exposed, and of a debt that might never be fully repaid.
"Thank you," Rex said, his voice dropping to a sincere, gravelly register. "For the whole truth."
"I know it cost you in more ways than one to give it to me in that order."
Lustia drew a breath, finally reassembling the fragments of her regal persona. Her voice regained its melodic strength, though the ghost of her earlier emotion still lingered in her eyes.
"You are welcome. But Rex... come back and say things like that more often."
’If you continue, I may start to actually enjoy these visits instead of merely orchestrating them."
"I will keep that in mind," Rex said.
As the divine realm began to dissolve around him, Rex allowed himself a single, quiet exhale, the sound of a man who had just survived a psychological ambush and emerged with a weapon in hand.
’The pieces are set,’ he thought as the darkness rushed in. ’ I have my alibi, I have my target, and I have the truth...’
’Now, all that’s left is to break them...’
His consciousness plunged downward, tearing through layers of astral energy until the familiar, crushing weight of physical reality returned.
He returned to his body.

’The pieces are set,’ he thought as the darkness rushed in. ’ I have my alibi, I have my target, and I have the truth...’
’Now, all that’s left is to break them...’
His consciousness plunged downward, tearing through layers of astral energy until the familiar, crushing weight of physical reality returned.
He returned to his body.

chapters.title: Chapter 879. I’ve Been Awake A Different Amount Of Time Than You Can Calculate
paragraphs: The guest room at the Starlight household was draped in that particular shade of pre-dawn gray, a liminal space where the world felt suspended between the exhausted silence of night and the inevitable intrusion of day. The light was weak and uncertain, filtering through the curtains like ash.
On the left side of the bed, Elizabeth slept. She possessed the focused stillness of someone who didn’t merely rest but recovered with military efficiency.
Her breathing was deep, rhythmic, and measured the steady pulse of a body that had been pushed to its limits and was now methodically rebuilding itself.
Rex sat on the right side of the bed, a shadow among shadows.

He remained motionless, monitoring his own internal state. The mark on his wrist hummed at its baseline, steady and quiet, the frantic energy of the divine domain visit having receded like a retreating tide.

In the background of his consciousness, his Presence Manipulation was working silently, a passive engine of signature management that shaved off the jagged edges of his aura. For the first time since the Sable Island integration, Rex could feel the difference; he was no longer broadcasting a signal to the world but absorbing it, becoming a ghost within his own skin.
His eyes drifted to the translucent glow of the system’s notification queue hovering in his peripheral vision.
[SYSTEM NOTIFICATION]
[PREGNANCY CONFIRMED Elizabeth Von Starlight.]
[FREE SKILL SELECTION UNLOCKED.]
[BUT YOU ALREADY CHOSE PRESENCE MANIPULATION.]
Rex stared at the words. ’Pregnancy confirmed... good shit...’
’Better late than never... I guess...’
A cold, pragmatic calculation flickered through his mind. This wasn’t about sentiment; it was about the brutal mathematics of power.

He looked at Elizabeth’s sleeping form, the woman who held the keys to the Starlight legacy, and then back at the screen. The cost of advancement had always been blood, sweat, or something far more intimate. He had paid that price. Now, it was time to collect.

With a deliberate swipe of his mental interface, he bypassed the standard skill trees and dove straight into the restricted catalog. His eyes searched for the one prize that would turn the tide against the gods.
’Let me check it...’
[DIMENSIONAL MANIPULATION FULL POTENTIAL]
[Complete navigation and operation across all known dimensional registers.]

[Enables: Detection of dimensional boundaries and layer transitions; controlled crossing of dimensional thresholds without standard teleportation anchors; operation within dimensional layers outside the primary physical plane; creation of localized dimensional pockets for storage or containment; and identification of dimensional workings applied to an area or target.]
[COMBINATION WITH TELEPORTATION: Extends teleportation’s navigation to all dimensional layers, including divine domains and their adjacent spaces.]

[PASSIVE FUNCTION: Constant awareness of the dimensional composition of the current environment detects temporal, spatial, or divine workings applied to the environment before their effects are felt.]
[KEY APPLICATION: Navigation to and from divine domains without divine invitation or sponsorship.]
[FREE SELECTION APPLIED AT NO COST.]
[DO YOU WANT TO FEEL IT?]
’Fuck yeah...’
The moment he committed to the selection, the world didn’t change; it unfolded.

It began as a searing pressure behind his eyes, followed by an invasive, terrifying expansion of his senses. It felt as though his consciousness was being stretched thin across a canvas that was far larger than he had ever imagined.
Then, the pressure snapped into clarity.
The integration was violent in its precision.
Suddenly, the room was no longer just four walls and a ceiling. His perception tore through the physical matter, revealing the hidden architecture of reality.
It was as if he had been blind to the very air he breathed, and now, suddenly, he could see the wind.
Through the new lens of his passive awareness, the room became a complex tapestry of overlapping strata.

First, there was the obvious: the physical plane of wood, fabric, and flesh. But beneath that, like veins beneath skin, he could see the shimmering, sickly residue of the temporal workings, the fading echoes of Kaeleth’s manipulation that still clung to the island like radioactive dust.
Even after Lustia’s counterfrequency had attempted to scrub it clean, the scars remained visible to him now.
And deeper... still deeper than time itself, he saw the foundation. The raw, grinding dimensional architecture of the island’s substrate, the ancient bones upon which this reality was built.
Rex didn’t flinch. He simply observed.
His mind, already hardened by years of tactical warfare, began to catalog the new data with ruthless speed. He wasn’t just seeing the room anymore; he was reading the blueprint of existence.
He read it.
The foundational layer’s dimensional composition was not some simple mineral map or a geological readout of bedrock. That was peasant-level perception.

What Rex saw now was something far more profound and unsettling; it was the skeletal framework of reality itself. He was looking at the specific dimensional architecture that eight hundred years of divine maintenance had woven into the island’s very base.
It was a cathedral of spacetime, constructed and reinforced by celestial hands.
And there, bleeding through the immaculate design like an infection in a clean wound, was the foreign signature.

It was the temporal working. Even after Lustia’s counterfrequency had attempted to sterilize the area, the residue remained a jagged, unnatural distortion that didn’t belong to the island’s natural rhythm.
It was a scar across the fabric of existence.
’Kaeleth’s work,’ Rex thought, his mind cataloging the anomaly with cold, surgical precision. ’A foreign imposition... An artificial graft onto a divine body.’
He didn’t recoil from the wrongness of it. Instead, he leaned into the new sensation, noting the specific frequency of the distortion, its phase shift, and its residual decay.
He filed it away in the deepest vaults of his memory.
Now, he wouldn’t just be affected by temporal anomalies; he would see them coming before they even touched his skin. He would see the trap before the trigger was pulled.

The coldness of his tactical mind retreated momentarily as he turned his gaze toward Elizabeth. The dimensional layers continued to swirl around her: the physical flesh, the spiritual aura, and the subtle displacement of space where her body met the mattress.

He looked at her with the quiet, focused attention of a predator taking inventory of something precious not out of sentimentality, but out of a fierce, possessive need to protect the assets he had claimed.
He leaned down, his movement fluid and silent, and pressed his lips to her temple. The contact was feather-light, a ghost of a touch that wouldn’t disturb her fragile equilibrium.
"Sleep," he murmured against her hair.

His voice was a low vibration, carrying a rare, genuine warmth and a vulnerability he never permitted himself to show the world. This wasn’t a performance for an audience; it was the truth he only allowed himself in the dark.
"You earned it twice over last night."

Elizabeth stirred, a soft, unconscious sound escaping her throat, a small noise of comfort that acknowledged the presence of warmth without breaking the veil of sleep. Rex lingered for one heartbeat longer, letting the image of her peace anchor him before he straightened, the mask of the soldier snapping back into place.

He dressed with the mechanical, lethal efficiency of a man who operated on a different clock than the rest of humanity. The grey morning light meant nothing to him; his internal gears were already grinding toward the next objective.
The door opened with a soft click.
The hallway was not empty. Lily and Diana were both standing there, positioned in the corridor like sentinels.
Whether it was coincidence or the uncanny sixth sense that develops in people who have learned to read the shadows of those they care about, Rex didn’t care. Their presence alone spoke volumes.
They knew. They could feel the charged atmosphere clinging to him like smoke from a battlefield.
Their eyes locked onto his.
"You look like you’ve been awake for three hours longer than you should have been," Lily said, her voice carrying an edge of concern she couldn’t quite disguise.
Rex’s expression remained impassive, his eyes reflecting the hollow exhaustion of someone who had just traversed dimensions.
"I have been awake for a different amount of time than either of us can easily calculate," he replied.
It wasn’t a deflection; it was the literal truth. His subjective experience had been fractured by the divine domain, stretched and compressed by forces they couldn’t comprehend.
Diana didn’t ask about his sleep. She didn’t ask about the time.

She simply watched him with that flat, terrifyingly perceptive stare, the look she used when she knew the surface story was a lie designed to protect the deeper wound. She could see the way his shoulders held tension that wasn’t just physical but existential.
"Are you... fine?" she asked, her voice quiet but carrying the weight of an interrogation.
Rex didn’t offer her the comfort of a lie. He didn’t have the time for it.
The new power thrumming in his veins demanded action, and the pieces of the puzzle were still scattered across the board.
"Yes," Rex said, his voice cutting through the morning stillness like a blade. "I need information."
