She dipped her shoulder beneath his arm, the motion so fluid it seemed almost supernatural, and as she passed inside his guard, she unleashed a devastating combo that demonstrated why she was the matriarch of this bloodline.
WHIP THUD CRACK!
First came a lightning-fast left palm strike to Rex’s diaphragm, forcing the air from his lungs in a wet wheeze.
Before he could recover his breath, she spun on her heel, converting the momentum into a vicious elbow strike that caught Rex squarely across the cheekbone.
CRACK.
The sound of cartilage protesting echoed off the stone walls.
Without pausing for even a heartbeat, Aurelia followed through with a snap kick to his kneecap, her shin connecting with the joint with the force of a breaking sledgehammer.
THWACK.
Rex grunted as his leg buckled, but his training took over.
Instead of falling, he used the pain as fuel.
As Aurelia pulled back to reset, Rex twisted his torso mid-collapse, driving an uppercut upward that caught her under the chin.
BOOM.
Aurelia’s head snapped back violently, blood spraying from her mouth as her teeth collided.
She stumbled backward, but Rex was already on her.
He lunged forward like a wounded bull, his fists becoming a blur of relentless aggression.
He threw a left jab to her eyes to obscure her vision, followed immediately by a thunderous right cross to her ribs.
PUFF.
CRUNCH.
Aurelia gasped as a rib visibly shifted under the impact, but her fury only intensified.
"Is that all?" she roared through the blood.
She met his aggression with a counter combo that left the onlookers speechless.
As Rex swung for a finishing blow, Aurelia caught his wrist with both hands, twisting her body sideways to redirect his power into the floor.
While he was off balance, she drove two consecutive knee strikes into his solar plexus, THUD THUD, each one more precise than the last, designed to collapse his diaphragm.
Rex staggered, his vision swimming with dark spots, but as she moved in to capitalize, he threw his forehead forward in a brutal headbutt.
CRUNCH.
The sound of their skulls colliding was sickening.
Both fighters recoiled, blood streaming down their foreheads.
Rex’s nose was a ruin of broken cartilage, and Aurelia’s left eye began to swell shut instantly.
They stood three feet apart for a moment, both swaying, their breathing coming in ragged, desperate gasps that sounded like tearing cloth.
"You... fight like a demon," Aurelia spat, wiping a thick smear of blood from her lips.
Her voice was thick, her composure shattered, replaced by something far more dangerous: genuine bloodlust.
"And you..." Rex growled, spitting a glob of crimson onto the floor, "...fight like you were born from a massacre."
Rex charged again, but this time it was different.
He wasn’t just throwing strikes; he was weaving them together.
He feinted a high kick, drawing Aurelia’s guard up, then immediately dropped low, driving a vicious leg sweep that caught her ankles.
As she stumbled, he came up with a rising elbow aimed at her throat.
WHOOSH.
Aurelia twisted her neck at the last millisecond, the elbow grazing her carotid artery.
She retaliated with a spinning back fist that caught Rex across the temple.
WHACK.
His head snapped sideways, blood spurting from a fresh gash on his scalp.
The fight descended into a beautiful, horrifying chaos.
They became two storms colliding in the center of the hall.
Rex would land a crushing blow to her ribs (THUD), and Aurelia would respond with a flurry of three precise punches to his kidney and liver (BAM BAM BAM), forcing him to double over.
When he would grab her, attempting to crush her throat with his forearm, she would drive her thumbs into his pressure points, seeking to paralyze his grip.
GRIND.
SNAP.
THUD.
The floor beneath them was no longer wood; it was a slick, crimson mire of sweat and blood.
Every time they landed a solid hit, the sound reverberated through the room like a gunshot.
The elite unit watched in stunned silence, recognizing that they weren’t watching a spar; they were watching two gods tearing each other apart to see who would claim the throne.
Rex’s knuckles were split open, dripping blood onto Aurelia’s torn training gear.
Aurelia’s breathing was a series of broken sobs of exertion, her ribs bruised to the bone.
Yet neither would yield.
Each time one stumbled, the other would press the advantage with renewed ferocity, their movements becoming more primal, less technical, and infinitely more deadly.
